brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of food (a high-fat, high-calorie meal) on the PK of a single oral dose of budesonide delayed release tablet in healthy participants. The main questions it aims to answer are :

(1) Does a high-fat, high-calorie meal significantly alter the plasma exposure (Cmax, AUC) of budesonide following oral administration of D23A? ( 2) How does food intake affect the absorption rate (Tmax, Tlag) and other PK parameters of D23A? Researchers will compare the plasma PK parameters of D23A administered under fasted conditions versus fed conditions to see if a high-fat, high-calorie meal has a significant impact on the bioavailability and absorption kinetics of D23A .

Participants will receive a single oral dose of 16 mg D23A (4 tablets) in each period of the crossover study, with one period under fasted conditions and the other under fed conditions (after consuming a high-fat, high-calorie meal) . The study will also monitor and record any adverse events (AEs) to evaluate the safety and tolerability of D23A under fed conditions .

brief_summary: This study tested whether changing how quickly patients expect to heal after cataract surgery changes how quickly their vision recovers. Adults having cataract surgery in both eyes were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups watched a short video of their surgeon before each surgery and completed short daily surveys afterwards. In one group, the video gave somewhat faster recovery timeframes and the surveys asked patients to notice day-to-day changes in their vision. In the other group, the video gave standard recovery timeframes and the surveys asked about activities and mood. Visual acuity was measured at routine clinic visits 1 day, 1 to 2 weeks, and 3 months after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change in best-corrected visual acuity at 1 day
Change in best-corrected visual acuity at 1 to 2 weeks
title: Manipulating Temporal Expectations to Accelerate Recovery After Cataract Surgery

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of intermittent pneumatic compression, local heat, and mechanical vibration applications on recovery following high-intensity anaerobic exercise in elite female basketball players. Recovery levels of the athletes will be evaluated through blood lactate concentration, countermovement jump performance, perceived recovery status, and perceived muscle soreness. The study will compare the effects of different recovery application sequences on post-exercise recovery indicators.
interventions: Local Heat and Mechanical Vibration (Venom 2 Leg)

brief_summary:
The objective of this prospective cohort study is to evaluate marginal bone loss and peri-implant health in patients with single dental implants requiring prosthetic rehabilitation, comparing conventional and digital methods for fabricating implant-supported crowns over a 24-month period.

The primary questions the study aims to answer are:

Are there differences in marginal bone loss between implant-supported crown rehabilitations fabricated using conventional versus digital workflows?

Are the prosthetic fabrication methodology, crown design, and abutment characteristics associated with differences in peri-implant health and outcomes related to osseointegration?

How do peri-implant clinical parameters and marginal bone loss relate to the patients' oral health-related quality of life?

The researchers will follow two groups of patients: one undergoing prosthetic rehabilitation via conventional impression-taking, and the other via digital scanning. The projected sample size is 32 patients, with 16 in each group.
lead_sponsor: Pontificia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul
primary_outcomes: Peri-implant bone loss
title: Influence of Prosthetic Characteristics of Implant-Supported Crowns on Peri-implant Health and Osseointegration: A Comparison Between Digital and Conventional Workflows.

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of intravenous tenecteplase (rhTNK-tPA) in patients with acute ischemic stroke managed under different transfer models. Treatment decisions are made by the treating physicians as part of routine clinical care and are not assigned by the study protocol. Clinical information, imaging findings, laboratory results, treatment data, and functional outcomes will be collected. Participants will be followed for 90 days. The primary effectiveness outcome is the modified Rankin Scale score at 90 days. Safety outcomes include symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours and all-cause mortality at 90 days.
primary_outcomes: Modified Rankin Scale Score at 90 Days
title: Tenecteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke Under Different Transfer Models

brief_summary: This study aims to test whether transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIs) can improve upper limb motor function in patients in the early subacute stage after acute ischemic stroke. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either active tTIs treatment or sham stimulation. All subjects will receive routine rehabilitation. The treatment will be given once daily for 20 consecutive days. Researchers will assess upper limb motor function before treatment, during the intervention and after the treatment course to compare the effect between the two groups. Safety will also be monitored throughout the study.
interventions: Sham Transcranial Temporal Interference Stimulation (Sham tTIs)
primary_outcomes: Fugl-Meyer Assessment of Upper Extremity (FMA-UE)
title: Temporal Interference Stimulation for Upper-Limb Motor Recovery in Early Subacute Stroke

brief_summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant public health issue with an increasing prevalence worldwide. In patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) in particular, various factors-such as chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, nutritional disorders, and micronutrient deficiencies-can negatively affect muscle health and physical function. Selenium, an essential trace element with potent antioxidant properties, has been shown to be present at low levels in these patients and may be associated with muscle strength. Sarcopenia and frailty are critical clinical conditions in HD patients that diminish quality of life and increase the risk of hospitalization and mortality. This study aims to evaluate the relationship between serum selenium levels, sarcopenia, and frailty in patients undergoing chronic hemodialysis, and to investigate whether selenium levels might serve as a potential biomarker for these clinical conditions.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the effects of head-mounted display (HMD)-based immersive virtual reality (VR) simulation on enema administration skills, learning satisfaction, and self-confidence among nursing students.

The study was conducted with 68 first-year nursing students at a public university in Türkiye during the spring semester of the 2025-2026 academic year. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=34) or a control group (n=34).

Both groups received standardized theoretical and practical training in enema administration, including a video demonstration and hands-on practice using a low-fidelity patient mannequin. In addition to standard training, the intervention group participated in a single 10-15-minute HMD-based immersive VR simulation session. The control group received standard training only during the study period.

Enema administration skills were assessed using a 30-item skills checklist, while learning satisfaction and self-confidence were evaluated using the Student Satisfaction and Self-Confidence in Learning Scale. Assessments were conducted at the initial measurement and at one-month follow-up.

The study aimed to determine whether incorporating HMD-based VR simulation into conventional nursing skills education improves students' clinical skill performance, learning satisfaction, and self-confidence.
primary_outcomes: Enema Administration Skill Performance
title: Effects of HMD-Based Virtual Reality Simulation on Enema Administration Skills in Nursing Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether using a special green dye called indocyanine green (ICG) during minimally invasive rectal cancer surgery can help surgeons assess blood flow to the bowel and reduce leakage from the surgical connection between two ends of the bowel.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does using ICG fluorescence imaging reduce the risk of leakage from the bowel connection after surgery?
* Does ICG imaging help surgeons identify areas of the bowel with poor blood flow and decide whether the planned bowel connection needs to be changed?

Researchers will compare ICG fluorescence-guided assessment with conventional visual assessment of bowel blood flow during rectal cancer surgery.

Participants will:

* Undergo planned minimally invasive rectal cancer surgery as part of their treatment.
* Be randomly assigned during surgery to either the ICG fluorescence imaging group or the standard care group.
* Undergo postoperative imaging to check the bowel connection, usually around postoperative day 5 and approximately 4 weeks after surgery.
* Be monitored for postoperative complications during their hospital stay and for 30 days after surgery.
* Attend a follow-up assessment approximately 30 days after surgery.
lead_sponsor: Basavatarakam Indo American Cancer Hospital & Research Institute
primary_outcomes: Total Anastomotic Leakage Rate
title: FLuorescent Angiography in REduction of Anastomotic Leak in Rectal Cancer Surgery

Seventy participants experiencing gastrointestinal discomfort associated with GLP-1 RA use will be randomized to receive either Oxxynea® or a matching placebo once daily for six weeks.

Participants will complete questionnaires at Baseline, daily for the first 14 days, and at the end of Weeks 2, 4, and 6. The primary measure is change in gastrointestinal comfort assessed by the Gastrointestinal Quality of Life Index (GIQLI). Secondary measures include quality of life, participant-perceived product benefits, and specific GI symptom changes (nausea, abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, and constipation).

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate whether reduced heart function is associated with differences in stomach contents before elective coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery will be divided into two groups based on their left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), a measure of how well the heart pumps blood: patients with an LVEF below 40% and patients with an LVEF of 40% or higher. Before surgery, the researchers will use ultrasound to examine the stomach. They will assess the presence and amount of stomach contents using the Perlas grading system and ultrasound measurements of the gastric antrum. The main objective is to compare gastric ultrasound findings between the two groups. The researchers will also evaluate estimated gastric volume and the frequency of stomach findings associated with a higher risk of aspiration during anesthesia.

Participants were followed for 12 weeks after switching, with a final follow-up at 24 weeks. The study also assessed feasibility (recruitment, retention, and visit attendance) and used interviews with participants and service-agency staff to understand acceptability and how a tobacco harm reduction program could fit into existing housing and clinic services.
interventions: Nicotine replacement therapy (patch, gum), both arms

brief_summary: Measurement instruments in physiotherapy practice play a fundamental role in clinical decision-making, treatment planning, and the objective monitoring of treatment effectiveness. Conducting this study is necessary to reveal current practices, identify measurement and evaluation habits, assess the extent to which evidence-based practice is reflected in clinical care, and contribute to the development of educational content and clinical standards. Furthermore, the findings will provide a scientific basis for planning strategies aimed at promoting patient-centered and objective assessment approaches.
primary_outcomes: Frequency of Use of Clinical Assessment and Outcome Measurement Tools Among Physiotherapists in Türkiye

brief_summary: Research shows that how well oxygen moves from the lungs into the blood (called lung diffusing capacity) is linked to a person's aerobic fitness and endurance training. People who exercise regularly often have different lung and heart responses than people who do not. The exact reasons for these differences are still unclear. This study will test one possible explanation: highly trained people may handle changes in the amount of blood returning to the heart differently than people who are not trained. We want to learn how the blood vessels in the lungs react when the amount of blood entering the heart changes, and how this reaction is affected by fitness level. To do this, we will change how much blood returns to the heart by applying air pressure around the legs, similar to a light vacuum. These changes are expected to be similar to what happens when someone moves from lying down to standing up.
interventions: Lower body positive and negative pressure

The study aims to determine the comparative analgesic effectiveness of these two regional anesthesia techniques and contribute to optimizing postoperative pain management after total laparoscopic hysterectomy.

brief_summary:
Primary objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of relaxation techniques combined with the Pilates method versus the Pilates method alone in improving perimenopausal and menopausal symptoms.

Specific objectives:

* To determine the baseline status of the patients regarding menopausal symptoms.
* To evaluate changes in symptoms, emotional well-being, interoceptive awareness, quality of life, and health-related sleep quality among participants following the intervention in both treatment groups.
* To compare changes in symptoms, emotional well-being, interoceptive awareness, quality of life, and health-related sleep quality among participants following the intervention between the two treatment groups.
* To examine the participants' level of adherence to the intervention programs.

Task 1 (T1): Patient recruitment and informed consent forms. Task 2 (T2): Initial assessment. Task 3 (T3): Interventions. Task 4 (T4): Final assessment post-treatment. Task 5 (T5): Medium-term assessment one month post-treatment. Task 6 (T6): Data analysis. Task 7 (T7): Publication and dissemination.

Approximate number: 50 participants, 25 per group.

Recruitment: Women over 40 years of age in the perimenopausal or menopausal stage, presenting with associated symptoms; recruited at a physiotherapy center via referral from the center's physiotherapists.

Methodology: Assignment to a control group (Pilates, 2 sessions/week) and an intervention group (Pilates + relaxation techniques, 2 sessions/week) for 10 weeks. 60-minute sessions led by physiotherapists.

Variables will be measured using: MENQOL for menopausal symptoms and quality of life; SF-12 for general quality of life; DASS-21 for anxiety, depression, and stress; PSQI for sleep quality; and MAIA for the multidimensional assessment of interoceptive awareness; adherence will be tracked via a diary.

Data analysis: Normality will be assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. A descriptive analysis will be performed using percentages for qualitative variables and mean ± SD or median and IQR for quantitative variables. Between-group comparisons will be conducted using the Student's t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, and the Chi-square or Fisher's test, as appropriate. Intervention effectiveness will be analyzed using an intention-to-treat approach, comparing pre- and post-intervention changes in the short and medium term via paired t-tests or the Wilcoxon test. Repeated-measures ANOVA will be used for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance will be set at p \< 0.05. Analysis will be performed using SPSS v29.0.
conditions: Women Over 40 Years of Age in the Perimenopausal or Menopausal Stage, Presenting With Associated Symptoms
primary_outcomes: menopausal symptoms and quality of life using MENQOL
General quality of life using SF-12
Anxiety, depression, and stress using DASS-21
Sleep quality usign PSQI
Multidimensional assessment of interoceptive awareness using MAIA
title: Relaxation Techniques and Pilates for Menopause Symptoms

brief_summary: Dermatophyte infections of the skin, hair and nails are common in Pakistan, and treatment failure with standard antifungal drugs is increasingly reported. Local laboratory data on how dermatophytes respond to terbinafine and itraconazole are limited. This study will collect skin scrapings, hair or nail samples from consecutive dermatology outpatients with KOH-confirmed dermatophytosis, grow the fungi in culture, and test each isolate against terbinafine and itraconazole using the standard CLSI M38 broth microdilution method. The study will report the proportion of Trichophyton isolates with an elevated terbinafine minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), the MIC distributions of both drugs, and the species involved, and will explore whether elevated terbinafine MICs are associated with clinical features such as disease duration, previous antifungal use and topical corticosteroid use. Participation does not change treatment; the study only tests samples in the laboratory.

brief_summary:
Wheelchair users must be able to move around freely and access public buildings and transport, but current accessibility standards (e.g. maximum 8% ramp slope) are based on limited scientific evidence about the real biomechanical and perceived difficulties encountered by manual wheelchair users in daily life.

Manual wheelchair propulsion is not purely a motor activity: it also involves cognitive and emotional demands (attention, trajectory planning, stress and frustration management) that contribute to a mental workload. This cognitive dimension is still rarely integrated into biomechanical evaluation protocols.

This exploratory (pilot) study aims to test the feasibility of a protocol combining objective biomechanical data (shoulder joint loading estimated from motion capture and instrumented handrims) with the subjective experience of participants (perceived physical demand from the NASA-TLX questionnaire, perceived exertion from the Borg scale), during standardized and more realistic manual wheelchair propulsion tasks, including tasks performed under an added cognitive load (auditory-verbal 2-back dual task).

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis with cefazolin is necessary to prevent surgical site infections in adult women undergoing breast-conserving surgery (lumpectomy or partial mastectomy) for breast cancer. Specifically, the trial aims to establish whether surgery without antibiotic prophylaxis is non-inferior to surgery with cefazolin prophylaxis in terms of surgical site infections within 30 days after surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the rate of surgical site infections within 30 days after surgery without antibiotic prophylaxis non-inferior to that observed with cefazolin prophylaxis?
* How does surgery without antibiotic prophylaxis affect postoperative complications, including antibiotic-related adverse events, and the subsequent management of surgical site infections?

Researchers will compare preoperative cefazolin prophylaxis (2 g administered intravenously) with placebo (0.9% saline solution) to determine whether surgery without antibiotic prophylaxis is non-inferior to surgery with cefazolin prophylaxis in preventing surgical site infections. A total of 1,600 participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups. Neither the participants nor the healthcare professionals involved in their care will know which treatment has been administered.

Participants will:

* Undergo breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer, with or without a sentinel lymph node procedure, as part of their usual care.
* Receive a single intravenous administration of either cefazolin or placebo before the surgical incision.
* Receive information about the signs and symptoms of surgical site infections and how to contact the study team if an infection is suspected.
* Be contacted by telephone approximately 15 and 30 days after surgery to assess the occurrence of surgical site infections and other postoperative complications.

No additional hospital visits are required specifically for the study.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with any surgical site infection (SSI)
title: Evaluation of the Effect of Antibiotic Prophylaxis During Lumpectomy for Breast Cancer: Prospective Randomised Double-blind Noninferiority Study of Placebo vs Cefazolin

brief_summary:
The purpose of this global multicenter confirmatory study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Quantum-Inspired Intervention (QII), a novel non-invasive neurodevelopmental protocol, in children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).

Autism Spectrum Disorder involves complex neurodevelopmental dynamics characterized by challenges in emotional regulation and adaptive functioning. Existing clinical paradigms primarily rely on pharmaceuticals for secondary symptom control or behavioral methods aimed at external behavioral modification, while interventions targeting core functional shifts remain limited. Grounded in a quantum-inspired conceptual framework aimed at addressing foundational adaptive processing, QII integrates AI-enabled, fine-grained characterization of each child's needs with a proprietary quantum-inspired intervention protocol delivered by trained practitioners. While fully elucidating the fundamental mechanisms will require extended scientific timelines, the urgent needs of individuals and families make confirming tangible, real-world functional efficacy the paramount priority.

Preliminary case reports of the QII protocol observed encouraging signals in emotional stabilization and spontaneous communication. Building on these initial findings, this study systematically evaluates the efficacy of QII at scale in an expanded, multicenter cohort. Eligible participants will be randomized to receive either the standardized QII protocol over a defined period or a waitlist control, with the waitlist control arm offered QII following completion of the primary analysis. The primary endpoint evaluates improvement in the autism-related symptom or functional difficulty identified as the primary intervention target at baseline, as measured by the Clinical Global Impression-Improvement (CGI-I) scale; changes in irritability and behavioral dysregulation, as measured by the Aberrant Behavior Checklist-Irritability Subscale (ABC-I), are evaluated as a secondary endpoint.All efficacy endpoints are assessed by independent clinicians blinded to group allocation. Caregivers may report any adverse event or safety concern at any time and may request to stop the intervention at any time; adverse events are also recorded at scheduled study assessments.
primary_outcomes: Clinical Global Impression-Improvement (CGI-I) Score for the Primary Intervention Target
title: Evaluation of a Novel Quantum-Inspired Intervention (QII) for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Global Confirmatory Study

brief_summary: Breast cancer is one of the world's most common cancers in females. Most of the chemotherapy protocols used to treat breast cancer involve doxorubicin. Doxorubicin has a very significant antitumor effect on breast tumors. One of the obstacles that hinders the use of doxorubicin is cardiotoxicity. Although many agents are used to address this issue, only dexrazoxane is FDA-approved. One suggested pathway for doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity is due to calcium imbalance. Calcium ions are very important in controlling the heart's function. Nicorandil is an anti-anginal agent that shows cardioprotective effects against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in preclinical trials. Not only that, but preclinical studies on rats and mice have also shown that it has antitumor and augmenting effects on doxorubicin's anticancer properties. Here in our trial, the impact of the nicorandil will be assessed on breast cancer patients. The chosen method will be a parallel, open-label, randomized clinical trial. The selected sampling method will be stratified blocks based on radiotherapy and HFA-ICOS baseline scores. The sample size will be 146 patients, who will be randomized using a premuted block. The primary parameter will be the ejection fraction. The secondary parameters will include cardiac troponins, creatine kinase myocardial band, safety assessment of nicorandil use on the gastrointestinal and cardiovascular systems, quality of life after nicorandil use, cost-effectiveness and cost-utility of nicorandil, and the quality of life and baseline cardiac scoring system.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the effect of nicorandil on left ventricular ejection fraction in breast cancer patients receiving doxorubicin.
To evaluate the safety of nicorandil
title: The Impact of Using Nicorandil for the Prevention of Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an experimental, personalized cancer vaccine called TMV vaccine is safe and to find the best dose to study in future trials. The study includes adults with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that has come back in or near the same area after earlier treatment, and who are planning to have surgery to remove it. The study will also test the vaccine together with toripalimab-tpzi, an approved immunotherapy drug.

The TMV vaccine is made from each participant's own tumor tissue. Small particles taken from the surface of the tumor cells have 2 immune-boosting proteins added to them, to help the immune system recognize and attack the cancer.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the TMV vaccine safe, and what medical problems do participants have after receiving it?
* What is the best dose of the TMV vaccine to use in future studies?
* Is the TMV vaccine safe when given together with toripalimab-tpzi before and after surgery?

The study has 2 parts.

In Part 1 (Phase 1a), participants will:

* Have tumor tissue collected during their planned surgery, which is used to make their personal vaccine
* Receive the vaccine as small injections into the skin every 2 weeks for 3 doses, starting after they recover from surgery
* Visit the clinic about once a week for 8 weeks for checkups, blood tests, and safety monitoring
* Have scans every 3 months and be followed for up to 3 years

The first participants will receive the lowest dose. Later groups will receive higher doses only if the lower dose is found to be safe.

In Part 2 (Phase 1b), participants whose tumors test positive for a marker called PD-L1 will:

* Have a biopsy to collect tumor tissue for their personal vaccine
* Before surgery, receive 2 doses of the vaccine and up to 2 doses of toripalimab-tpzi through a vein
* After surgery, receive 1 more dose of the vaccine and continue toripalimab-tpzi every 3 weeks for up to 1 year
* Have regular checkups, blood tests, and scans, and be followed for up to 3 years

Researchers will also study blood and tumor samples to learn how the immune system responds to the vaccine.

brief_summary:
Oral squamous cell carcinoma is one of the significant public health concerns and the most prevalent malignancies affecting the head and neck region globally. The primary risk factors for this cancer include tobacco usage, alcohol consumption and increasing incidence of human papillomavirus infections (HPV). The incidence of oral squamous carcinoma has been rising among young populations and the prognosis among young and older patients remains a debated issue. However, recent studies(1) found that there is no significant difference in tumor stage or grade based on age and the premalignant disorders represent an early stage in the evolution of cancer that characterized by molecular alterations and clonal expansions that progress to malignancy. This entails that age specifically is not a determining factor in aggressiveness and treatment outcomes of Oral squamous cell carcinoma, emphasizing the need to focus on other factors that influence prognosis of this condition(2).

Premalignant disorders may involve detectable molecular alterations in blood cells and tissues, somatic mutations in key genes included DNMT3A and TET2 have been recognized in leukocytes of healthy individuals indicating a risk of future malignancy. There is a growing area of research where a comparison of hematological parameters like Total leukocytes Count (TLC), neutrophils and monocytes in OSCC patients versus those with premalignant disorders. The measurement of these blood markers provides an insight into immune response and systemic inflammation associated with malignancy progression. The evaluation and finding of Total leukocytes count, neutrophils and monocytes offered important and valuable prognostic information and also helped in distinguishing between malignant and premalignant conditions in the population. The monitoring of genetic mutations in blood cells of individuals could provide a non-invasive method to identify individuals at risk and help in better outcomes(3).

The leukocyte counts particularly neutrophils, monocytes and total leukocytes count (TLC) have been investigated for cancer progression and patient immune response. Elevated levels of these blood cells have been observed in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma indicating systemic inflammation and alterations in immune system that are associated with malignancy, whereas in premalignant conditions alterations in these parameters in the patients indicate immune response to cellular changes with key probable to predict malignant transformation. Comparing the levels of these blood counts in oral squamous cell carcinoma patients and those with premalignant lesions provide valuable awareness and insights into immunological, inflammatory processes involved in the early stages of cancer progression(4).

There are approximately 3% of all the malignancies affecting around 270,000 people globally in annual rate. A significant amount of proportion of oral squamous cell carcinoma cases develops from premalignant disorders of the oral cavity including leukoplakia and oral submucous fibrosis, which has very high rate of malignant transformation(5). Therefore, hematological parameters would be explored as potential biomarkers for early detection of OSCC and its prognosis. Studies have revealed that quantitative changes in blood biochemistry and hematology occur during tumor initiation and progression, highlighting their potential role as the tumor markers(6).

Therefore, despite the advancement of cancer therapy the prognosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma remained poor. This is largely due to the late diagnosis of the condition, however early detection is critical for improving patient outcomes and some recent research revealed various biomarkers and hematological parameters as a potential diagnostic tool and explored that immunological and hematological changes have been observed particularly alterations in total leukocyte count, neutrophils and monocytes and these changes have been investigated as an indicators of cancer progression. This underscores the importance of studying immune and also hematological detailed profiles in Oral squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions(7).

The purpose of the study is to assess and compare particular hematological parameters in individuals with premalignant conditions and those with squamous cell carcinoma. The study focus on hematological profile specifically Total leukocyte count (TLC), neutrophil count and monocyte count. By comparing these hematological markers in the patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma and the patients with pre-malignant lesions, therefore this study seeks to identify a distinct pattern that distinguishes between malignant and premalignant conditions. This comparative study aims to understand immune and inflammatory profiles of patients between two groups of study participants.
interventions: CBC will be required to assess the level of TLC (Total Leucocyte Count), Neutrophils and Monocytes in patient of oral squamous cell carcinoma and oral pre malignant conditions, using different stains
primary_outcomes: To compare the mean value of neutrophils, monocytes and total leucocyte count in oral squamous cell carcinoma and pre malignant patients.
title: Comparison of TLC (Total Leucocyte Count), Neutrophils and Monocytes in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Pre-malignant Disorders

brief_summary:
This clinical research study is investigating whether the EXOPULSE Suit, a wearable device that delivers electrical stimulation, can help improve movement difficulties caused by spasticity in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS).

The main goal of the study is to evaluate the effect of the EXOPULSE Suit on functional mobility, with particular focus on walking ability and balance. The study will also assess the safety of the device by monitoring any adverse events that occur during the study.

Researchers will additionally evaluate the effects of the EXOPULSE Suit on:

* Pain
* Hand and finger dexterity
* Fatigue
* Quality of life

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of the stimulation programs being evaluated in the study. Some participants may receive a sham (placebo) stimulation. Neither the participants nor the study staff performing the assessments will know which stimulation program a participant has been assigned to during the study. This approach, known as blinding, helps ensure that the study results are as objective and reliable as possible.

Participants will use the EXOPULSE Suit for one hour every other day during a 4-week home-use period. Clinical assessments will be performed before and after the treatment period to evaluate changes in mobility and other symptoms.

It is important to note that individuals may experience the stimulation differently. Some participants may clearly feel the stimulation, while others may feel it only slightly or not at all. Not feeling the stimulation does not necessarily indicate which study group a participant has been assigned to, and a treatment effect may still be possible even when the stimulation is not perceived.

To ensure meaningful study results, participants are encouraged to use the EXOPULSE Suit as instructed throughout the study period, even if they do not notice a sensation of stimulation or an immediate improvement in their symptoms.

The study uses an adaptive design, meaning that an interim analysis will be performed during the study to determine the number of participants needed to reliably evaluate the study objectives.
primary_outcomes: Balance responder rate: Percentage of patients achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in balance, as measured by the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), in the treatment group compared with sham-control group.

Walking responder rate: Percentage of patients achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in walking ability, on the transformed 0-100 Multiple Sclerosis Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12), in the treatment group compared with the sham -control group.
title: Evaluating the Effects of the EXOPULSE Suit on Mobility, Walking Ability, and Balance in People With Multiple Sclerosis

brief_summary:
Mental illness stigma among nursing students can undermine the quality of care that people with psychiatric conditions receive, and many students feel unprepared for psychiatric practice. This randomized controlled trial will examine whether an AI-based psychiatric simulation programme can reduce stigma and improve readiness for psychiatric nursing practice among fourth-year nursing students at the Faculty of Nursing, Alexandria University, Egypt. It will also test whether these effects are explained by students' sense of psychological safety during simulation-based learning.

Two hundred students will be randomly allocated 1:1 to either the intervention or the control arm. Both arms will receive the standard psychiatric-mental health nursing curriculum. The intervention arm will additionally complete five individual AI-simulation cases (one per week over five weeks, about 15-20 minutes each), covering depression with suicide risk, mania, schizophrenia, substance use disorder, and borderline personality disorder with self-harm. Each case includes a structured interview with a simulated patient, a standardized stigma-trigger statement, automated feedback, and an opportunity to retry.

Mental illness stigma, readiness for psychiatric practice, and psychological safety will be measured online at two time points: baseline and immediately after the fifth case. Intervention-arm students will also answer two open-ended questions, analyzed thematically to help explain the quantitative findings.
primary_outcomes: Mental illness stigma: Opening Minds Stigma Scale for Health Care Providers (OMS-HC) total score
Readiness for psychiatric practice: adapted 21-item Preparedness instrument (Dela Rosa and Maniago, 2018) total score
title: AI Simulation to Reduce Stigma and Enhance Psychiatric Readiness in Nursing Students

brief_summary:
This study Neqpiaput Iinruugut ("Our Food is Medicine"), will test if a tribally designed Indigenous food sovereignty intervention can lower the risk of coronary heart disease in Alaska Native adults ages 18 to 65 years old. Designed by Yup'ik Elders, the 12-month intervention combines Calricaraq, an established Elder-designed behavioral health program rooted in ancestral wisdom, with hands-on activities focused on traditional foodways. About 150 adults in three Alaska Native communities will take part. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the intervention lower participants' Framingham Risk Score, a measure of a person's chance of developing heart disease?
* Do cultural strengths, such as cultural identity, Yup'ik wellness, community connectedness, social support, and family cohesion, grow with participation, and does that growth help explain changes in heart disease risk?
* Does the intervention improve Indigenous food sovereignty, including practice and value of traditional foodways and the cultural systems that support them?

Researchers will compare communities receiving the intervention to communities waiting to start it (a dynamic wait-listed design) to see if the intervention lowers Framingham Risk Scores.

Participants will:

* Attend monthly in-person Calricaraq gatherings in their community for 12 months
* Attend quarterly hands-on food sovereignty workshops
* Join a Facebook group that shares resources and supports engagement between in-person sessions
* Have blood pressure and cholesterol measured and complete surveys during the study, including 6 months after the intervention ends
* Be invited to take part in focus groups at 12 and 18 months
primary_outcomes: Change in Framingham Risk Score
title: Neqpiaput Iinruugut (Our Food Is Medicine): A Tribally Driven Food Sovereignty Intervention to Reduce Heart Disease Risk in Alaska Native Adults

brief_summary:
This study aims to identify factors linked to spinal cord injury after aortic repair. The aorta is the body's main artery. The repairs studied use a fabric-covered tube, called a stent graft, placed inside the aorta. Sometimes, blood flow to the spinal cord is reduced after these procedures. This is called spinal cord ischemia and can cause leg weakness or loss of feeling.

Researchers will review existing medical records and scans from adults aged 18 or older. They will compare patients who developed spinal cord ischemia with those who did not. They will examine patients' health, repair details, blood pressure during the procedure, medicines used, and blood vessels supplying the spinal cord.

The study will also describe when this complication develops, how it is treated, and how patients recover. It will assess survival and time spent in hospital. The findings may help identify patients at greater risk and inform future prevention strategies.

This study uses information collected during routine care. Patients will not need additional tests, scans, treatments, or visits.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Spinal Cord Ischemia
title: Risk Factors for Spinal Cord Injury After Minimally Invasive Aortic Repair

brief_summary:
Gait-MAP is a prospective, randomized, single-blind clinical trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of an Intensive Interactive Gait Training (IIGT) program in adults with neurological conditions associated with pyramidal syndrome and walking limitations. The study aims to determine whether interactive treadmill-based gait training, incorporating body-weight support, virtual reality exercises, and real-time visual and auditory feedback, can improve walking efficiency, endurance, functional mobility, and participation in daily and community life compared with conventional gait rehabilitation.

Participants will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group (EG), receiving IIGT, or the control group (CG), receiving conventional gait rehabilitation with comparable duration, frequency, and intensity. The experimental intervention will consist of approximately 15 sessions of 45 minutes and will include task-specific exercises and controlled environmental challenges designed to reproduce real-life walking situations. Both interventions will be integrated into the participants' standard multidisciplinary rehabilitation program.

The primary outcome is the Cost of Walking (CW), assessed through cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), including oxygen consumption (VO₂), carbon dioxide production (VCO₂), and other physiological parameters. Secondary outcomes will assess walking endurance and mobility, motor function, fatigue, balance confidence, independence, quality of life, and community participation using an ICF-based assessment framework. Measures include the 6-Minute Walk Test, 10-Meter Walk Test, Timed Up and Go and dual-task TUG, Functional Ambulation Classification, Modified Barthel Index, SF-36, Activities-specific Balance Confidence Scale, and Walking Handicap Scale. Participants will be assessed at baseline, during treatment, at the end of treatment, and at a 3-month follow-up. The study is expected to determine whether IIGT can enhance walking efficiency and endurance while promoting greater autonomy and transfer of rehabilitation gains to real-life mobility and social participation.
primary_outcomes: Cost of walking - CW
title: Interactive Intensive Gait Training in Walking Limitations

brief_summary:

Mobile clinics may help overcome these barriers by bringing diagnostic testing and specialist support directly to rural communities.

This cluster-randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate a mobile clinic-supported, village doctor-led model for HF screening and integrated management among older patients with AF in rural China. Mobile clinics equipped with echocardiography and NT-proBNP testing will support HF screening, and subsequent management will be tailored according to HF status. The study will evaluate whether this model can improve the detection of HF and reduce adverse cardiovascular events compared with routine management.

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot randomized controlled trial is to investigate whether the Integrated Psychoeducation Program reduces internalized stigma and improves related outcomes in adults with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, and whether the program is feasible to deliver in a community mental health setting.

The main question it aims to answer is: Do participants who receive the program show a greater reduction in internalized stigma from pre-test to post-test than participants in a waitlist control group who continue treatment as usual? Researchers will also examine changes in self-esteem, hopelessness, and psychological flourishing, whether changes are maintained at 3-month follow-up, and attendance and retention rates.

Participants in the intervention group will attend 8 weekly group sessions that combine psychoeducation, an expressive writing exercise, and breathing/relaxation exercises. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue treatment as usual and will be offered the program after the study. All participants will complete questionnaires before the program (pre-tests), after the program (post-tests), and 3 months after the post-tests (3-month follow-up).

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to understand how the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), a region at the front of the brain, guides decisions about whether to pursue a possible reward when doing so also carries a risk of loss, and how this process is altered in depression. People with depression are often less motivated by rewards and more sensitive to potential losses, leading them to avoid situations that others would approach. The OFC is thought to play a central role in these "approach or avoid" decisions, but how it normally does so, and what goes wrong in depression, is not well understood.

This study asks two questions: (1) How does activity in different parts of the OFC signal the decision to approach or avoid? (2) Does this activity differ in people with depression in a way that explains a bias toward avoidance? We hypothesize that the medial OFC (toward the middle of the brain) signals approach, the lateral OFC (toward the side of the brain) signals avoidance, and that in depression the medial OFC signal is weakened, tipping decisions toward avoidance.

Participants are adults who are hospitalized with stereo-EEG (sEEG) electrodes already placed in the brain by their medical team, either to locate the source of seizures in epilepsy or as part of a separate clinical trial for treatment-resistant depression. The electrodes are placed for clinical reasons only, not for this study. During their hospital stay, participants complete a short, game-like computer task (about 20 minutes per session) in which they repeatedly choose whether to approach or avoid options that offer different chances of reward and loss. Their choices and reaction times are recorded along with brain activity from the existing electrodes, and participants rate their mood before each session.

The researchers will compare OFC activity during approach versus avoid decisions, use mathematical models of decision-making to measure how strongly each participant weighs rewards and losses, and compare participants with and without depression. No drugs, devices, or brain stimulation are given as part of this study. The findings are intended to guide the development of more targeted brain-stimulation treatments for treatment-resistant depression.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Orbitofrontal Cortex High-Frequency Activity (70-150 Hz) Between Approach and Avoidance Decisions
title: Understanding the Neural Underpinnings of Risk-Taking Behavior in Psychiatric Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of two generative artificial intelligence technologies (an interactive AI video avatar vs. a personalized GPT) in enhancing professional English learning, overall tool satisfaction, and attitudes toward generative AI. The study will be conducted in undergraduate third-year nursing students enrolled in a professional English course at a university health sciences faculty in Türkiye.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is there a significant difference in professional English knowledge test scores between nursing students using an interactive AI video avatar and those using a personalized GPT?
* Is there a significant difference in attitudes toward generative AI in English learning between students using the interactive AI video avatar and those using the personalized GPT?

When someone has bladder cancer, abnormal cells form in the bladder and can spread to other parts of the body if not treated. Bladder cancer that has spread outside the bladder is called advanced or metastatic bladder cancer.

When cancer develops, a pathologist examines a sample of the tumour under a microscope to see which cells the cancer started from. This is called the cancer's histology. Most bladder cancers begin in the cells that line the inside of the bladder and are called urothelial cancers. Less commonly, bladder cancer can develop from other cell types.

The purpose of this study is to examine the types of histology that adults with advanced or metastatic bladder cancer have. The researchers will also describe the demographics (information such as age, sex and race) clinical characteristics and outcomes of those patients.

This is a real-world study, not a clinical study. This means that researchers will look at what happens when patients receive the treatments prescribed by their own doctor as part of their usual healthcare treatment. The study will include patients' information from the database who:

* Started their first treatment after 01 Apr 2023.
* Were 18 years of age or older when they were diagnosed with advanced disease.

brief_summary: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of mortality from advanced liver disease, accounting for 47.9% of cirrhosis-related deaths and 30% of hepatocellular carcinoma-related deaths annually. In China, both per capita alcohol consumption and the prevalence of ALD (approximately 5.15%) are on the rise, making ALD an increasingly significant public health burden. Alcohol-associated fatty liver disease (AFLD), the initial and most reversible stage of ALD, is pathologically characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation, mild hepatocellular injury, and low-grade inflammation. It can progress to alcoholic hepatitis, and in some patients, advance to hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis, or even hepatocellular carcinoma. Currently, there is no established effective pharmacotherapy for AFLD; although alcohol abstinence remains the optimal strategy for disease reversal, sustained abstinence is often difficult to achieve among individuals with alcohol dependence. Dietary protein source may independently influence metabolic health beyond total protein intake. Plant proteins (primarily derived from legumes and cereals) are rich in arginine, glutamine, and fiber-associated bioactive compounds, whereas animal proteins (mainly from dairy and poultry) are abundant in branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and sulfur-containing amino acids. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that, compared with animal proteins such as casein, plant proteins more effectively attenuate high-fat- or alcohol-induced hepatic steatosis by upregulating hepatic PPAR-α expression and suppressing SREBP-1c activity. Human intervention studies further suggest that long-term higher intake of plant protein is associated with lower hepatic fat content and reduced risk of insulin resistance. However, no randomized controlled trial has yet directly compared the effects of high-purity plant protein versus animal protein supplementation on clinical outcomes in patients with AFLD under isocaloric and isonitrogenous conditions. Therefore, this study aims to conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of plant protein versus animal protein supplementation within an isocaloric dietary framework on liver function, hepatic fat content, and glucose-lipid metabolism in individuals with AFLD. The findings will elucidate the efficacy and underlying mechanisms of protein-source modulation in ameliorating AFLD, thereby providing population-based evidence and strategic guidance for health promotion in this patient population.
primary_outcomes: Intrahepatic lipid (IHL)
title: High-Plant-Protein-Diet or High-Animal-Protein-Diet for Improving Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease

brief_summary:
Developmental language disorder (DLD) is a condition that affects children's ability to learn and use language. These difficulties can affect communication, learning, and participation in everyday activities. Although DLD is relatively common, we still do not fully understand the brain processes that contribute to these language learning difficulties. A better understanding of these processes could help researchers identify children who may benefit from support earlier and develop new approaches to improve language learning.

One possible explanation for the language learning difficulties experienced by children with DLD is that they have difficulty identifying patterns in the speech they hear. To understand speech, children must learn to recognize where words begin and end, which sounds and words tend to occur together, and how words combine to form meaningful sentences. Children can learn many of these patterns simply by listening to language, even without being explicitly taught the rules. It is possible that difficulties in detecting and learning these patterns may contribute to the language challenges experienced by children with DLD.

This project focuses on a brain process called neural entrainment. Neural entrainment occurs when the brain's electrical activity synchronizes with patterns in the information we receive from the environment. For example, when we listen to speech, our brain activity can align with the rhythms and timing of the sounds. This synchronization may help the brain organize incoming information and identify important patterns that support learning. Previous research has linked neural entrainment to learning, and early findings suggest that children with DLD may show differences in how their brain activity synchronizes with speech. However, we do not yet know whether these differences are related to their learning difficulties or whether influencing these brain rhythms could help them learn better.

The proposed study will investigate these questions in 160 children, ages 5 to 6, with and without DLD. We will measure children's brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG), a safe, noninvasive method that records electrical activity through sensors placed on the scalp. The study will focus on a relatively slow brain rhythm known as the delta frequency band. This rhythm is of particular interest because previous research suggests that it may play a role in processing the timing and structure of speech.

The first goal is to determine whether children's brain rhythms are related to how well they learn different aspects of language. Children will participate in two learning activities. In the first activity, they will listen to a continuous stream of speech containing made-up words. The words will not be separated by pauses, so children will need to use patterns in the speech to figure out which sounds belong together and where the words begin and end. In the second activity, children will learn language through a more naturalistic task involving short stories and pictures. They will listen to sentences made up of unfamiliar words while viewing pictures that illustrate the stories. The sentences will follow a consistent structure, with an actor performing an action on another person or object. Together, these activities will allow us to investigate whether neural entrainment is associated with learning at both the word and sentence levels.

The second goal is to determine whether rhythmic sound stimulation can influence brain rhythms and learning. Before each learning activity, children will hear one of two types of sound sequences. One condition will involve rhythmic stimulation designed to match the slow timing of the delta frequency band. The other will serve as a comparison condition without the same regular rhythm. Each child will experience both conditions across two study sessions. We will compare children's learning between the two conditions to determine whether rhythmic stimulation improves their ability to identify words and learn sentence patterns. They will also examine whether any learning benefits are associated with changes in neural entrainment.

If neural entrainment is found to be consistently associated with children's ability to learn language patterns, it may eventually help researchers develop an objective measure to support the early identification of DLD. If rhythmic stimulation also improves learning, it could provide a foundation for developing new approaches to support language development. These applications will require further research, but the proposed study represents an important step toward understanding the brain mechanisms involved in learning and identifying new ways to support children who experience language difficulties.

brief_summary: Breastfeeding provides important short- and long-term benefits for maternal and infant health. Breastfeeding self-efficacy, defined as a mother's belief in her ability to initiate and maintain breastfeeding, is a key determinant of breastfeeding success. This randomized controlled trial is currently evaluating the effect of a solution-focused approach (SFA) training program on breastfeeding avoidance and breastfeeding self-efficacy in primiparous mothers. Eligible participants are randomly assigned (1:1) to an intervention group, which receives four weekly, 45-minute online group sessions based on solution-focused techniques (e.g., scaling questions, reframing, EARS, miracle question, and exception-seeking questions), or a control group, which receives routine standard postpartum care. Breastfeeding avoidance and breastfeeding self-efficacy are measured before and after the intervention using validated scales. However, in the early postpartum period, some mothers and infants may experience difficulties with breastfeeding, which can negatively affect the initiation and continuation of breastfeeding. Difficulties encountered during breastfeeding can undermine a mother's confidence in her ability to breastfeed and negatively affect breastfeeding success. Therefore, it is important to develop nursing interventions aimed at supporting breastfeeding. Finger-feeding is one of the alternative feeding methods used to support sucking skills and is thought to be beneficial in supporting the breastfeeding process.

This study was designed as a randomized controlled experimental study to determine the effect of nurse-led finger-feeding support on mothers' breastfeeding self-efficacy and early-stage breastfeeding outcomes.

The purpose of this clinical study is to learn about the safety and effects of the study medicine (called PF-08161842) and how it is processed by the body. This is the first time PF-08161842 will be given to people.

This study is seeking healthy adults:

* 18 to 64 years of age or 65 to 85 years of age
* Who are in generally good health
* Who meet study conditions for body weight and body mass index (BMI)

Participants will receive either PF-08161842 tablets or matching placebo tablets. Placebo tablets do not contain active medicine. In some study groups, participants will receive a single dose of study medicine. In other study groups, they will receive the study medicine for 14 days. The tablets will be taken by mouth at the study clinic.

We will compare the experiences of people receiving the study medicine with those of people who do not. This will help researchers determine if PF-08161842 is safe and how it affects the body.

Participants will stay at the study clinic for several days so the study team can closely monitor their health. The study will include physical examinations, checks of blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, and breathing. It will also include blood and urine samples and heart tracing tests (ECGs). Researchers will assess how the body processes the study medicine. Some participants will also have lumbar punctures (spinal taps) to collect small samples of fluid from around the brain and spinal cord. The study team will monitor participants for any reactions throughout the study.

For people receiving a single dose, the study will last for about 9 weeks. For those receiving multiple doses the study will last for about 11 weeks. This includes screening, study visits, clinic stay, and follow-up contact after the last dose.

brief_summary: This study aims to determine the simultaneous effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) at two frequencies (30 Hz and 100 Hz) compared to sham stimulation on cognitive functions, dual-task performance, and interoceptive accuracy in healthy adults. taVNS non-invasively activates vagal afferent fibers through electrical stimulation of the outer ear (cymba conchae and tragus), which are exclusively innervated by the auricular branch of the vagus nerve. Its proposed mechanism involves activation of the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine system and insular/prefrontal projections, providing a putative neurobiological basis for cognitive modulation. Ninety healthy volunteers (18-45 years) will be randomly assigned to one of three parallel groups: sham taVNS (n=30), active 30 Hz taVNS (n=30), or active 100 Hz taVNS (n=30). Each participant completes two sessions separated by one week: Session 1 (baseline, no stimulation) and Session 2 (experimental, stimulation active). Assessments include dual-task cost (3-Meter Tandem Walk Test with serial subtraction), executive function (Stroop Test), processing speed (Deary-Liewald Reaction Time Task), interoceptive accuracy (Heartbeat Counting Task), and heart rate variability (Polar H10). Sleep quality (PSQI), depression (BDI), physical activity (IPAQ-SF), and fatigue (Chalder Fatigue Scale) are measured at baseline as potential moderators. This is the first double-blind, sham-controlled study to simultaneously evaluate the effects of taVNS on these three constructs within a single experimental design, and the comparative frequency analysis (30 Hz vs 100 Hz) will contribute to parameter optimization for taVNS applications.

brief_summary: Cognitive problems are common after a stroke and must be identified early so that rehabilitation can be initiated to improve outcome. In 2015, a tool developed specifically to screen for cognitive deficits in stroke, the Oxford Cognitive Screen (OCS), was released. Despite the tool now being widely used internationally, we don't know how good it is at finding cognitive problems and know very little about how well it predicts recovery of cognitive problems. In this study, we will assess cognition in 240 stroke survivors using the OCS and detailed cognitive tests in both the early stage (within three weeks of stroke) and the chronic stage (6-9 months after stroke) to learn more about how well the tool does at measuring cognitive problems and predicting recovery. The study will also inform us on how large a percent of stroke survivors have cognitive impairments in the early stages after stroke and in the chronic stage of recovery.

brief_summary:
Transcutaneous spinal stimulation (TSS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation approach that delivers electrical stimulation to spinal nerve roots through electrodes placed over the spinal cord. TSS may support motor and functional recovery following spinal cord injury (SCI). However, therapeutic potential alone does not establish whether TSS can be feasibly integrated into routine rehabilitation. Clinical implementation introduces practical considerations including clinician training, device setup and operation, time, safety monitoring, acceptability, organizational resources, and compatibility with existing rehabilitation workflows.

This study will evaluate the feasibility of integrating TSS into two existing SCI rehabilitation programs at Parkwood Institute: outpatient upper- and lower-extremity functional electrical stimulation (FES) cycling using the Xcite system with TSS functionality, and routine inpatient physiotherapy and occupational therapy using the Stim2Go device. Evaluating TSS across two rehabilitation contexts will identify setting-specific barriers, facilitators, and implementation requirements.

The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility, safety, acceptability, and implementation strategies required to integrate TSS into outpatient FES cycling and inpatient SCI rehabilitation. Secondary objectives are to explore preliminary changes in clinical and functional outcomes and synthesize implementation findings into evidence-informed recommendations for TSS implementation.

A multi-methods, multi-intervention case series design will be used. Implementation will be guided by the Active Implementation Frameworks and a Training and Coaching Model. Feasibility will be evaluated using Bowen et al.'s Feasibility Framework and the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability, examining acceptability, demand, implementation, practicality, integration, and limited efficacy.

The study will recruit 15 adults with SCI and up to 10 clinicians. Ten patient participants will be recruited from the outpatient FES cycling program and five from inpatient SCI rehabilitation. Up to 10 clinicians who integrate TSS into participant care will also be recruited.

Outpatient participants will receive TSS during their regularly scheduled FES cycling sessions for four weeks. TSS will be delivered during routine 30-45-minute cycling sessions one to two times per week, targeting the cervical spine for upper-extremity cycling and lower thoracic/lumbar spine for lower-extremity cycling. Inpatient participants will receive TSS using Stim2Go during routine physiotherapy and occupational therapy for a minimum of four weeks, with a target of at least three TSS-assisted sessions per week. TSS will be embedded within usual rehabilitation activities, including transfer training, pre-gait and mobility training, activity-based therapy, and upper-extremity task-specific training.

Primary feasibility outcomes will include recruitment, attrition, intervention adherence, adverse events, and patient and clinician experiences. Following the implementation period, patient participants will complete an acceptability survey and semi-structured interview. Clinicians will complete an acceptability survey and participate in a focus group exploring feasibility, acceptability, barriers, facilitators, and lessons learned from integrating TSS into practice.

Exploratory clinical outcomes will also be examined. For outpatient participants, FES cycling outcomes from the four weeks before TSS will be compared descriptively with the four-week TSS period, including session time, distance, asymmetry, time without motor support, energy, power, crank velocity, and stimulation parameters. For inpatient participants, baseline and post-intervention outcomes will assess standing, walking, balance, mobility, endurance, upper- and lower-extremity strength, upper-extremity function when relevant, and independence in daily activities.

Quantitative feasibility, demographic, survey, cycling, and clinical data will be summarized descriptively and visually. Individual changes in inpatient clinical outcomes will be interpreted using minimal detectable change values where available. Qualitative interview and focus group data will undergo codebook thematic analysis informed by interpretive description to identify implementation experiences, barriers, facilitators, and recommendations.

This study will provide real-world evidence on whether and how TSS can be safely and feasibly incorporated into existing SCI rehabilitation services. Evaluating two devices across inpatient and outpatient contexts will identify practical implementation supports and setting-specific considerations not captured in laboratory-based research. Findings will inform recommendations to support adoption and sustained use of TSS across SCI rehabilitation settings in Canada.

Post-stroke epilepsy is estimated to affect approximately 30% of children who experience perinatal stroke. Although neonatal outcomes are relatively well characterized, the long-term course of epilepsy in this population and the relationship between initial stroke characteristics and subsequent epilepsy outcomes remain insufficiently studied.

The primary objective of this retrospective, multicenter, observational study is to characterize the long-term course of epilepsy in children who experienced an ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke before 28 days of age.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether a type of cell death called disulfidptosis plays a role in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) in adults aged 18 to 70. Researchers will do this by giving participants a study diet and four oral agents designed to block disulfidptosis, then checking whether liver blood tests change. This study is not designed to show that the combination treats PSC.

PSC is a long-term liver disease. In PSC, the bile ducts become inflamed and scarred over time. Bile ducts are small tubes that carry bile from the liver to the gut.

Researchers are testing a new idea about why bile duct cells are damaged in PSC. Cells need a balance of certain sulfur-containing building blocks and the energy to process them. When this balance breaks down, proteins inside the cell can stick together the wrong way. This can cause the cell's inner structure to collapse, and the cell dies. This type of cell death is called disulfidptosis. Researchers think disulfidptosis may contribute to bile duct damage in PSC.

This is a proof-of-principle study. This means it is an early, small study to test whether this idea is correct and worth studying further. Participants will follow a study diet and take four oral agents. Each agent was chosen because it may help protect cells from disulfidptosis:

Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), a natural antioxidant that helps cells manage stress N-acetylcysteine (NAC), which helps the body make glutathione, a natural antioxidant Nicotinamide riboside (NR), a form of vitamin B3 that helps cells make energy Metformin, a common diabetes medicine that changes how cells use sugar and energy

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does blocking disulfidptosis with the study diet and agents lower alkaline phosphatase (ALP)? ALP is a liver blood test that is often high in people with PSC.
2. Does it change other blood markers of liver health and inflammation?
3. What medical problems do participants have while on the study diet and agents?

There is no comparison group in this study. All participants will receive the study diet and all four agents.

Participants will:

1. Have a screening visit to check if they can join the study
2. Follow a study diet for the length of the study, with guidance from study dietitians
3. Receive help from the study to buy groceries that fit the study diet
4. Take photos of their meals and snacks using a phone app, so dietitians can review what they eat and give advice
5. Take the four study agents by mouth each day, starting at lower doses that are raised step by step over the first weeks
6. Visit the clinic in Boston about 11 times over about 18 weeks
7. Give blood samples at study visits to check liver tests, safety tests, and other markers
8. Answer questions about their health, symptoms, and any side effects

Researchers will watch closely for side effects throughout the study. If liver tests rise too much, researchers will follow set safety steps, which may include stopping one or more study agents. About 15 people will take part.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) From Baseline to Week 16
Percentage of Participants With ≥50% Reduction in Serum ALP at Week 16
title: FEAST and HOPE: Redox PSC Pilot Study

brief_summary:
This pilot study, the PilotPreAPAD study, will be carried out to check whether the key parts of the planned Prevention in asymptomatic Arterial Disease (PreAPAD) study will work in practice. In phase one, it will test the screening process for asymptomatic arterial disease and the prevalence of the disease in the screened population to help estimate the sample size needed before starting the larger randomized multi centre PreAPAD study. In phase two, the pilot will test the study protocol, the data collection tools and how acceptable the intervention will be to participants.

Peripheral artery disease is a disease where the arteries in the legs are narrowed by atherosclerosis causing pain in the affected limb during exercise and resting pain, ulcers and tissue loss in the more severe stage. Many people, however, are in the stage where they have no leg symptoms, even though they have narrowed arteries, the asymptomatic stage. Despite having no symptoms, they have almost double the risk of developing angina, heart attack, stroke, or dying prematurely-similar to those with more advanced disease.

The disease can be easily detected by measuring the blood pressure in the ankle and comparing it to the blood pressure in the arm. This is called the Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI). Measuring ABI makes it possible to identify people at higher risk of future heart and vascular events-risks that can potentially be prevented.

The PreAPAD study that is being planned aims to examine how preventive strategies affect heart- and other vascular events, quality of life, and disease progression in men and women with asymptomatic peripheral artery disease. Patients with diabetes, high blood pressure, COPD, or a history of smoking will be screened with ABI measurements to detect asymptomatic disease. The multimodal intervention that will be tested includes a health discussion with a nurse, participation in a health course, individualized exercise advice from a physiotherapist, exercise training, and medication to manage risk factors for cardiovascular disease if needed.

Approximately 96 players from six university women's volleyball teams will participate. The six teams will be randomly assigned to either the CR intervention group or the neutral volleyball referee-instruction group. Both groups will continue their regular volleyball training.

The CR group will receive weekly group sessions, brief pre-training exercises and homework focused on identifying and changing unhelpful thoughts in volleyball pressure situations. Participants will complete assessments before and after the 8-week study period. The assessments will include questionnaires measuring competitive state anxiety, trait sport anxiety, sleep quality and mental effort, together with standardized tests of serving, reception, spiking, blocking and defence.

The study will compare changes in anxiety and volleyball skill performance between the two groups. Participation is voluntary. The study involves no drugs or medical devices. Exercise and testing-related discomfort will be monitored, and participants may stop or withdraw from the study at any time without penalty.

brief_summary:
Introduction: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a global health challenge requiring effective, evidence-based interventions, such as Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT). Although clinical guidelines position individual CPT as a first-line treatment, evidence regarding its group format -despite it being the original modality- remains limited. Given the potential of the group format to optimize costs and improve access to treatment in high-demand health systems, evaluating its feasibility and clinical efficacy is a priority.

Objectives: The project proposes a phased research study focused on the implementation, scalability, and clinical impact of group CPT for women who are victims of gender-based violence and exhibit post-traumatic symptoms. Phase 1 (feasibility study) aims to evaluate the acceptability and feasibility of the group CPT protocol.

Methodology: Phase 1 will involve a non-randomized pilot study with female victims of gender-based violence with post-traumatic symptomatology; participants will receive 12 sessions of group CPT. Feasibility will be assessed in this phase based on recruitment rates, adherence, and participant satisfaction. Clinical outcomes (PTSD symptoms, general psychopathology, emotional regulation, and well-being) will be measured at three time points (pre-intervention, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up) using validated instruments.

Expected Results: "Healing Trauma"'s Phase 1 anticipates demonstrating high protocol feasibility and acceptability, as well as a clinically significant reduction in PTSD symptoms and the other measured variables. Furthermore, the project expects to produce a standardized intervention manual that could, in the future, be revised for adaptation and transfer to other psychological care units.

Significance: The project will provide an optimized and scalable group CPT protocol, facilitating the democratization of access to evidence-based treatments -particularly in high-demand health systems- while fostering clinical psychological practice grounded in evidence and scientific rigor.

Does postoperative Obstetric Quality of Recovery differ according to the neuraxial anesthetic technique used for cesarean delivery? Researchers will compare women receiving spinal anesthesia, epidural anesthesia, or combined spinal-epidural anesthesia to determine whether the anesthetic technique is associated with differences in postoperative quality of recovery.

brief_summary:
This study will test a CAR T-cell treatment combined with bevacizumab in children and young adults with relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, or osteosarcoma.

The CAR T-cell treatment, called GD2IL18CART, is made from a patient's own T cells. The T cells are genetically modified to recognize GD2, a molecule found on the surface of these cancers, and to release the immune-stimulating protein interleukin-18 (IL-18) when they encounter tumor cells. Bevacizumab is an antibody that blocks vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a protein that affects tumor blood vessels and may make it difficult for immune cells to enter tumors. Combining bevacizumab with GD2IL18CART may therefore help more CAR T cells reach the tumor and improve their antitumor activity.

The main goals of this study are to determine whether the combination can be given safely, identify a recommended dose of GD2IL18CART for use with bevacizumab, and look for early evidence of antitumor activity. The study will also examine blood and tumor samples to better understand how the treatment affects CAR T cells and the tumor environment.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and severity of adverse events
Dose-limiting toxicities and recommended dose - dose-finding part
Recommended dose of GD2IL18CART in combination with bevacizumab
Overall response rate at week 6 - dose-extension part
title: GD2IL18CART Combined With Bevacizumab for Relapsed and Refractory GD2-positive Solid Tumors
