brief_summary:
The use of digital learning technologies in health sciences education has increased substantially in recent years. In particular, video-based learning resources enable students to access educational materials regardless of time and location, thereby supporting more flexible and effective learning. However, teaching essential women's health clinical skills, including breast self-examination, vulvar self-examination, and gynecological examination, remains challenging because of limited laboratory practice, restricted clinical opportunities, and the need to protect patient privacy. These limitations may reduce students' opportunities for repeated practice and negatively affect both skill acquisition and long-term retention.

This project aims to develop EbeCast, a QR code-supported, vodcast-based digital learning platform designed to improve women's health clinical skills among midwifery students. The platform will include instructional vodcast videos, QR code-supported clinical skill cards, module-based assessments, and learning analytics. Students will be able to access educational materials anytime, review clinical procedures repeatedly, and progress at their own learning pace. Although previous studies have demonstrated the educational benefits of podcasts and vodcasts in health professions education, there is very limited evidence regarding QR code-supported digital learning platforms specifically designed for teaching women's health skills in midwifery education and evaluated through randomized controlled trials. Therefore, EbeCast is expected to provide an innovative and sustainable educational model for midwifery training.

The project is designed as a two-phase methodological and experimental study. During the first phase, educational materials, vodcast videos, QR code-supported skill cards, and the EbeCast digital learning platform will be developed. During the second phase, the effectiveness of the platform will be evaluated using a parallel-group randomized controlled trial with pre-test, post-test, and follow-up assessments. The study sample will consist of 64 third-year midwifery students (intervention = 32; control = 32) enrolled at the Faculty of Health Sciences, Karabük University. Both groups will receive the standard theoretical and laboratory curriculum, while the intervention group will additionally receive four weeks of access to the EbeCast platform. Data will be collected using a Personal Information Form, the Women's Health Clinical Skills Knowledge Test, Women's Health Clinical Skills Assessment Checklists, the Clinical Skills Self-Efficacy Scale, and platform usage analytics.

The project is expected to improve students' knowledge, clinical skill performance, self-efficacy, and long-term retention of women's health skills while providing an evidence-based, accessible, and sustainable digital learning model. Furthermore, the findings are expected to contribute to the digital transformation of midwifery education, provide an adaptable educational model for other health disciplines, and support future national and international scientific publications.
primary_outcomes: Change in Women's Health Clinical Knowledge Scores
Change in Breast Self-Examination Skill Performance
Change in Vulvar Self-Examination Skill Performance
Change in Gynecological Examination Skill Performance
title: Effects of EbeCast Digital Learning on Midwifery Students' Women's Health Skills

brief_summary: Diabetic foot ulcer is a common and disabling complication of diabetes mellitus. This randomized controlled trial will be conducted at Abbas Institute of Medical Sciences, Muzaffarabad to compare the efficacy of negative pressure wound therapy versus conventional moist wound dressing. A total of 60 patients aged 18-70 years with diabetic foot ulcer size greater than 3 cm will be randomly divided into two groups of 30 patients each. Group A will receive negative pressure wound therapy and Group B will receive moist wound dressing. Efficacy will be measured in terms of healing time and reduction in ulcer size after 4 weeks of treatment.

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) works to help people recover faster after laparoscopic surgery for stomach cancer. TEAS is a treatment that uses small electrical pulses through sticky pads on the skin. It does not use needles. The main questions it aims to answer are: Does TEAS help people pass gas (a sign that the digestive system is waking up) sooner after surgery? Does TEAS help lower pain after surgery? Does TEAS reduce the need for extra pain medication after surgery? Researchers will compare two groups to see if TEAS works better than a sham (inactive) treatment. Group 1 (TA group) receives real TEAS after surgery. Group 2 (SA group) receives a sham treatment at the same time points. All participants will receive the same standard pain relief and recovery care after surgery. Participants will: Be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to one of the two groups. Receive TEAS or sham treatment for 30 minutes starting 2 hours after waking from anesthesia, and then once daily each morning on the first 3 days after surgery. Rate their pain on a 0-10 scale at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after surgery. Complete quality-of-life and fatigue questionnaires before surgery, on day 4 after surgery, and 30 days after surgery. Have a follow-up visit or phone call 30 days after leaving the hospital. This study includes 104 adults aged 18 to 80 years who are scheduled to have laparoscopic surgery for stomach cancer at 8 hospitals in Shandong Province, China.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University
primary_outcomes: Time to First Flatus After Surgery
title: TEAS for Gastrectomy Recovery

brief_summary:
Peri-implant mucosal recession in the anterior esthetic zone is a clinically important complication because it can expose implant components, compromise esthetics, and reduce patient satisfaction. Soft-tissue thickness is considered one of the factors that may influence marginal mucosal stability, but the thickness required to minimize recession remains uncertain and may depend on implant position, facial bone thickness, tissue phenotype, surgical technique, and the timing of implant placement.

The central research question is: Is there a minimum peri-implant soft-tissue thickness at implant placement or restoration that is associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in midfacial mucosal recession over time?

An important distinction for the study is that an association between thicker tissue and less recession does not, by itself, establish a universal protective thickness threshold. The study should investigate both the continuous relationship between tissue thickness and recession and whether a clinically useful cutoff can be identified.
primary_outcomes: Midfacial Mucosal Recession
title: Association Between Peri-implant Soft Tissue Thickness and Midfacial Marginal Mucosal Recession

brief_summary:
This study compares two operations for stress urinary incontinence in adult women. Stress urinary incontinence means leaking urine during activities such as coughing, sneezing, laughing, or exercising. Women with both stress-related leakage and a sudden urgent need to urinate were also eligible if stress-related leakage was their main problem.

Both operations use the woman's own tissue to create a sling that supports the urethra, the tube that carries urine out of the bladder. One operation uses tissue from the vaginal wall, placed through openings in the pelvic bones near the groin (a transobturator vaginal wall sling). The other uses tissue from the strong layer covering the abdominal muscles (a rectus sheath pubovaginal sling). Neither operation uses synthetic mesh, although permanent supporting stitches are used.

Forty women at Kafrelsheikh University Hospitals, Egypt, were randomly assigned to one of the two operations, with 20 women in each group. Follow-up continued for six months after surgery.

The main question is whether the operations differ in preventing urine leakage during a cough test six months after surgery. The study also compares urinary symptoms, operation duration, urine flow, bladder emptying, and complications.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Objective Cure on Cough Stress Testing
title: Comparison of Two Autologous Sling Procedures for Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women

The primary outcome is self-rated likelihood of getting a flu vaccine this season (1-7), asked immediately after the session. Participants are asked at about 2 and 8 weeks whether they have been vaccinated. The study is powered for the intention outcome but not for vaccination. For vaccination, it estimates the effect, the base rate, and follow-up response, to size a later, larger trial.
primary_outcomes: Flu vaccination intention

brief_summary: Keloids are harmless, raised scars that develop when the body produces too much scar tissue after an injury, surgery, or other skin damage. They may grow beyond the original wound, become firm, red or purple, and cause itching. Treatment options include silicone dressings, pressure therapy, steroid injections, surgery, freezing, laser therapy, radiation, and other medicines. Steroid injections, especially triamcinolone, can soften and reduce the size and thickness of keloids. Radiofrequency microneedling is another treatment that uses very fine needles and controlled energy to create tiny channels in the skin. This may reduce keloid tissue, encourage healthier healing, and help steroid medication reach deeper into the scar
primary_outcomes: Compare the percentage of improvement in Detroit keloid scale score using combined Fractional microneedling radiofrequency (FMR)and steroid vs combined Fractional CO2 laser and steroid in keloid patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether a collagen filler improved facial wrinkles. The study product was injectable recombinant collagen freeze-dried fibers. Recombinant collagen is collagen made using genetic engineering. Participants were adults aged 18 to 65 with upper facial wrinkles. These included forehead lines, lines between the eyebrows, and lines beside the eyes.

The trial also studied the product's safety. The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* How many participants had fewer wrinkles 90 days after their final treatment?
* What side effects or other medical problems occurred during treatment and follow-up? Researchers compared the study product with Sunmax Collagen Implant I, another collagen filler. They compared how many participants improved in each group. Improvement meant wrinkles became at least one level less severe in every treated area. Researchers used a five-level scale to rate wrinkle severity.

The comparison allowed a small difference in improvement rates between the groups. Researchers set this limit before the trial began. They tested whether the study product stayed within that limit compared with the other filler.

Participants were asked to:

* Receive one of the two products, with their group chosen by chance.
* Receive three injection treatments, about 30 days apart.
* Record reactions in a diary for 14 days after each treatment.
* Attend follow-up visits about 30, 90, and 180 days after their final treatment.
* Have facial photographs taken for wrinkle assessments.
* Rate changes in their appearance and report any medical problems.
conditions: Upper Facial Lines (Glabellar Lines, Forehead Lines, & Lateral Canthal Lines)
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Improved Upper Facial Wrinkles
title: Recombinant Collagen Freeze-Dried Fibre for Upper Facial Wrinkles

brief_summary:
In-hospital cardiac arrest is a common phenomenon associated with high mortality rates. In the United States, 290,000 cases of in-hospital cardiac arrest among adult patients occur annually (1). The mean patient age is 66 years, and 58% are male. In the majority of cases (81%), the initial cardiac rhythm was non-shockable (asystole, PEA). The primary cause of arrest was cardiac (50-60%), followed by respiratory causes (15-40%) (1). Survival rates for these patients have risen over the past two decades; according to the GWTG-R registry, survival to hospital discharge was 25% in 2017, with 85% of survivors demonstrating a favorable neurological outcome (CPC score of 1 or 2; see details under "Objectives"). It is important to note that these figures vary across different countries, potentially due to differences in the patient populations studied (e.g., survival odds are better for cardiac-related arrest than for respiratory-related arrest; distinctions between internal medicine, surgical, cardiac, and trauma patients; the location of resuscitation-ICU vs. general ward, etc.) as well as cultural, social, and religious factors (e.g., awareness of DNR/DNI orders among the public and medical staff, specific national legislation, and patient preferences). ...the patient and their family regarding end-of-life care due to religious, cultural, or social reasons, etc.).

The GO FAR score (Good Outcome Following Attempted Resuscitation) is a clinical prediction tool that estimates the likelihood of survival to hospital discharge with a good neurological outcome (CPC score of 1) for patients who have undergone in-hospital resuscitation. This score was developed using data from 51,000 patients across 366 hospitals, based on the GWTG-R registry. It incorporates data known prior to cardiac arrest, enabling the medical team, the patient, and the family to formulate a plan in advance regarding the course of action should the patient experience in-hospital cardiac arrest. The data points include age, neurological status upon admission, multisystem trauma, acute stroke, hematologic-oncologic disease or metastatic cancer, sepsis with bacteremia, non-cardiac reason for admission, liver failure, admission from a nursing facility, hypotension or shock upon admission, renal failure, respiratory failure, and pneumonia upon admission. Subsequently, the GO FAR 2 score was developed; while it included the same data points, it slightly modified the scoring method and also incorporated a CPC score of 2 (2,3).

We aim to examine survival rates to discharge with a good neurological outcome following in-hospital resuscitation... At Meir Hospital, we are focusing on a specific patient population: those hospitalized in internal medicine wards. This group generally has a lower likelihood of surviving with intact neurological function (due to factors such as advanced age, non-cardiac causes of arrest, and parameters contributing to a "GO FAR" score that reflects a poor prognosis). Our working hypothesis is that the success rate of resuscitation for these patients is typically very low; attempting it may cause suffering to the patient and their family without offering a reasonable chance of survival with a favorable neurological outcome. Beyond this point-which we consider paramount for the patient-resuscitation attempts with poor prospects entail other consequences: financial costs, extended hospital stays, increased workload for medical and nursing staff, and reduced resource availability for other patients with better recovery prospects, among others. Carefully selecting patients with a higher likelihood of successful in-hospital resuscitation would not only improve outcomes but also prevent unnecessary suffering. To formulate a plan for the informed selection of these patients, this study aims to collect relevant data.
conditions: Survival to Discharge With Good Neurologic Outcome Among in Hospital Cardiac Arrest Patients
primary_outcomes: survival to discharge
title: Therapeutic Outcomes of In-Hospital Resuscitation of Patients Admitted to the Internal Medicine Wards

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether reduced everyday functioning before the acute illness and malnutrition help predict health outcomes in adults aged 65 years and older hospitalized with acute coronary syndrome (heart attack or unstable angina). About 270 patients (no more than 330) will be enrolled in two hospitals in Samara, Russia.

After their condition has stabilized, and within seven days of admission, researchers will ask patients (or a caregiver) about their everyday functioning before the illness. They will also measure weight, height and calf circumference, ask about recent weight loss and food intake, and use a short questionnaire to screen for risk of malnutrition. With separate consent, two extra tubes of blood (11 mL in total) will be taken during a routine hospital blood draw, without an additional needle stick, so that albumin and C-reactive protein can be measured later. Information about the illness and its treatment will be collected from medical records.

Participants will be followed for one year for death, heart attack, ischemic stroke and unplanned hospitalization for heart or vascular conditions. Their ability to perform everyday activities will be assessed again between days 366 and 395 after enrollment. This is an observational study: participation does not change the medical treatment patients receive.
primary_outcomes: Time to First Major Adverse Clinical Event

brief_summary: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is a highly heterogeneous condition, making precision mechanical ventilation challenging. Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) provides real-time monitoring of regional lung ventilation, but interpreting its complex spatiotemporal data relies on subjective clinical experience. This multicenter ambispective cohort study aims to develop and validate an all-in-one Artificial Intelligence Foundation Model (AutoEIT). The study consists of two phases: (1) A Retrospective Phase (data from 2020 to 2025, N=1000) to train the AutoEIT model using continuous EIT images and synchronous high-frequency ventilator waveforms; and (2) A Prospective Temporal Phase (January 2026 to December 2026, N=200) to rigorously test the model's performance in a real-world clinical setting. The AutoEIT model is a deep multi-task learning framework designed to simultaneously perform five core clinical tasks: (1) classify ARDS subphenotypes, (2) recommend individualized positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), (3) detect occult patient-ventilator asynchrony, (4) predict ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) ratio, and (5) continuously estimate the non-invasive PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio. Ultimately, this system aims to reduce ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) and improve precision respiratory care.

title: Development and Prospective Validation of the AutoEIT Foundation Model for ARDS

brief_summary:
Rationale:

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer in the world, and patients with stage IIIB-IV have a poor prognosis. EGFR mutations, especially the 19th amino acid deletion (19del) and the 21st amino acid L858R mutation, are the most common types of gene mutations in NSCLC. These mutations usually lead to overactivity of EGFR, thereby stimulating excessive proliferation of lung cancer cells. At present, the conventional treatment for such patients is mainly the use of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) for treatment. However, although EGFR-TKIs have achieved certain results in the treatment of NSCLC patients with EGFR mutations, their treatment effects are often difficult to sustain due to the resistance of patients to these drugs. Therefore, finding new treatment strategies to improve the survival rate and quality of life of such patients is an important current research direction. The results of many studies suggest that EGFR TKIs and anti-angiogenic drugs can inhibit tumors from different signaling pathways. EGFR-TKIs can inhibit the epidermal growth factor receptor pathway and inhibit tumor growth; anti-angiogenic drugs inhibit tumor angiogenesis by binding to vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). At the same time, the combination of the two has a synergistic effect. Both EGFR and VEGFR-2 signaling pathways can trigger downstream signaling pathways such as PI3K/AKT and RAS/RAF/ERK, affecting cell proliferation. EGFR activation can also drive HIF-1α upregulation, leading to VEGF gene expression. Many clinical studies have confirmed that the A+T treatment model can improve the efficacy of EGFR-positive NSCLC.

Methods:

This study is planned to adopt a mixed design. We will prospectively collect new patient data and retrospectively analyze existing patient data. In the prospective part, we will treat patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC with EGFR amino acid 21 L858R mutation and amino acid 19 deletion (19del) with a combination of ametinib mesylate (AUMOLERTINIB) and recombinant human endostatin (ENDOSTAR). In the retrospective part, we will extract the existing data of patients treated with AUMOLERTINIB alone from the hospital\'s electronic medical record system as a control group. The primary endpoint is progression free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints are objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), adverse events (AE), quality of life (EORTCQLQ-L13) score, anxiety and depression self-rating scale (HADS) and patient health questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9).

Route:

In the prospective part, we will perform genetic testing on patients to determine their EGFR mutation status. Then, we will treat patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC with EGFR amino acid 21 L858R mutation and amino acid 19 deletion with ametinib mesylate and recombinant human endostatin, and match the corresponding data in the hospital database. We will regularly follow up patients participating in the prospective study, collect data on their disease progression and survival, and perform statistical analysis on these data to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the combination therapy.

Expected:

We expect that the combination of ametinib mesylate and recombinant human endostatin can improve the survival rate and quality of life of patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC with EGFR amino acid 21 L858R mutation and amino acid 19 deletion. This is mainly because ametinib mesylate and recombinant human endostatin target EGFR hyperactivity and angiogenesis, two processes that play a key role in the development of NSCLC, respectively, so their combined use may produce a synergistic effect, thereby improving the therapeutic effect.
lead_sponsor: Three Gorges Hospital of Chongqing University
primary_outcomes: progression-free survival (PFS)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Almonertinib Combined With Recombinant Human Endostatin in the Treatment of Stage IIIB-IV Non-small Cell Lung Cancer

The clinical and biological data collected will enable the conduct of future research projects in collaboration with research units and partner laboratories of the CRMR SED-NV at the Raymond Poincaré University Hospital.

brief_summary:
Fatigue is a common and debilitating symptom of cirrhosis, the advanced stage of chronic liver disease. Around two-thirds of people with cirrhosis experience fatigue, which can affect their ability to carry out everyday activities and substantially reduce their quality of life. Despite this, the biological causes of fatigue in cirrhosis are poorly understood and there are currently no effective treatments specifically targeting this symptom.

Cirrhosis is associated with long-term changes in the immune system, including increased inflammation in the blood. Inflammation in the body can also affect the brain and may alter processes important for normal brain function. We therefore propose that increased inflammation in people with cirrhosis may contribute to the development of fatigue by affecting brain cells.

This study will recruit 50 people with stable alcohol-related cirrhosis: 25 experiencing clinically significant fatigue and 25 without clinically significant fatigue. Participants will attend a single study visit, during which information about their fatigue, mood, thinking abilities and liver disease will be collected, alongside a blood sample.

We will compare blood samples from participants with and without fatigue to identify differences in inflammation and immune function. We will then use the serum (the liquid component of blood) collected from participants to treat human brain cells grown in the laboratory. This will allow us to investigate whether blood from people experiencing fatigue affects the growth, development and survival of brain cells differently from blood from people without fatigue.

By combining measurements in patients with laboratory experiments, we aim to identify biological mechanisms that may contribute to fatigue in cirrhosis. In the longer term, this could identify potential targets for new treatments and improve our understanding and management of this currently undertreated symptom.
primary_outcomes: Circulating inflammatory marker concentrations
Peripheral blood immune cell phenotypes
Serum-induced changes in human hippocampal neurogenesis
title: Inflammatory and Neuroimmune Guided Investigation of Underlying Fatigue in Patients With Cirrhosis

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blinded controlled trial evaluates whether lidocaine with adrenaline reduces bruising (ecchymosis) more effectively than lidocaine without adrenaline among women undergoing contraceptive implant insertion or removal at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital. Bruising is common after these procedures and may contribute to stigma and concealment behaviors; adrenaline's vasoconstrictive effect may lessen bleeding, prolong anesthesia, and reduce bruising, but the two formulations have not been directly compared in this setting.

A total of 450 women aged ≥18 years will be enrolled and randomized 1:1 (sealed opaque envelopes) to receive either lidocaine with adrenaline or lidocaine without adrenaline during implant insertion or removal. Participants and outcome assessors will be blinded. During the procedure, blood loss, heart rate, blood pressure, and pain will be recorded. Post-procedure follow-up lasts 7 days: participants submit standardized photos of the procedure site via Line OA on Day 3 and Day 7 for bruise assessment and report pain onset and satisfaction with wound appearance/healing.

Risks include transient effects potentially related to adrenaline (e.g., restlessness, palpitations, flushing, dizziness, brief increases in heart rate or blood pressure) and typical minor procedure-related effects (pain, mild bleeding, temporary discomfort). Vital signs will be monitored before and up to 30 minutes after anesthetic administration. Photo submission carries minimal privacy risk; images and data will be coded and stored securely with access limited to authorized personnel. If an adverse event is related to study participation and instructions were followed, medical costs and reasonable loss-of-time compensation will be covered. No insurance is provided.

No direct benefit to participants is expected, but findings may improve clinical practice by reducing bruising and enhancing patient satisfaction with contraceptive implant services. Participation is voluntary; withdrawal is permitted at any time without affecting medical care. Collected data will be anonymized; investigators, the sponsor, and authorized ethics/regulatory bodies may review records as permitted by law. Data will be destroyed after study completion; no biological samples will be stored.

Each weekly module includes a micro-learning video, an audio-guided exercise, an interactive digital tool, and a daily one-minute micro-practice, covering psychoeducation, mindfulness and somatic regulation, cognitive reappraisal, self-compassion, meaning-making, social support, practical coping, and relapse prevention. Control participants receive usual workplace orientation and routine hospital support and are offered the app after the final assessment.

Moral injury, burnout, secondary traumatic stress, psychological distress, and resilience will be measured with self-report scales at baseline, immediately after the intervention (week 8), and at one-month follow-up (week 12).

brief_summary:
Background Spinal anaesthesia is the preferred anaesthetic technique for most elective Caesarean deliveries; however, maternal hypotension following spinal anaesthesia remains very common and may be associated with maternal nausea and vomiting, reduced uteroplacental perfusion, and adverse fetal acid-base changes.

Several vasopressors have been used for the prevention and treatment of spinal anaesthesia-induced hypotension. Ephedrine has traditionally been used because of its combined α- and β-adrenergic effects. However, its indirect sympathomimetic action and placental transfer have raised concerns regarding maternal tachycardia and fetal metabolic effects.

Norepinephrine is a potent α-adrenergic agonist with modest β-adrenergic activity. It has increasingly been investigated as an alternative vasopressor for Caesarean delivery because it can effectively maintain maternal arterial pressure with less maternal tachycardia than ephedrine. Randomized studies comparing norepinephrine and ephedrine have demonstrated effective prevention of spinal hypotension with norepinephrine and, in some studies, more favourable neonatal acid-base variables.

Phenylephrine is widely used internationally for this indication; however, because of its limited availability in the Egyptian market, norepinephrine represents a potentially practical alternative in the local setting.

The present study is designed to compare prophylactic continuous infusions of norepinephrine, ephedrine, and a combination of norepinephrine and ephedrine for prevention of spinal anaesthesia-induced hypotension during elective Caesarean delivery. Maternal haemodynamic effects and neonatal outcomes, including umbilical cord blood gas analysis, will be assessed.

Aim of the study To compare the efficacy and safety of prophylactic continuous infusion of norepinephrine, ephedrine, and their combination in preventing spinal anaesthesia-induced hypotension during elective Caesarean delivery.

Primary outcome The incidence of maternal hypotension from initiation of spinal anaesthesia until delivery, defined as:Systolic blood pressure (SBP) \<90 mmHg.

Secondary outcomes Maternal outcomes

1. Number of hypotensive episodes.
2. Duration of hypotension.
3. Number of rescue vasopressor boluses required.
4. Total dose of study vasopressor administered.
5. Incidence of hypertension, defined as SBP \>140 mmHg.
6. Incidence of maternal bradycardia, defined as HR \<50 beats/min.
7. Incidence of nausea and vomiting.
8. Incidence of shivering.

Neonatal outcomes Apgar score at 1 and 5 minutes. Umbilical arterial pH. Umbilical arterial PaCO₂. Umbilical arterial bicarbonate. Patients The study will include healthy pregnant women, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I, with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy at ≥36 weeks of gestation, scheduled for elective Caesarean delivery under spinal anaesthesia.

After approval by the institutional Ethics Committee and obtaining written informed consent, eligible patients will be randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups using computer-generated randomization and sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes.

Group N - Norepinephrine Norepinephrine concentration: 4 µg/mL Group NE - Combination Norepinephrine concentration: 2 µg/mL plus Ephedrine concentration: 2 mg/mL Group E - Ephedrine Ephedrine concentration: 4 mg/mL Anaesthetic technique All patients will have an 18-G peripheral intravenous cannula inserted before transfer to the operating theatre.

On arrival in theatre, standard monitoring will be established, including ECG, non-invasive blood pressure, heart rate and pulse oximetry.

Baseline haemodynamic measurements After allowing the patient to rest in the operating theatre, three consecutive measurements of SBP and HR will be obtained before spinal anaesthesia at 1-minute intervals.

The mean of the final two measurements will be considered the patient's baseline SBP and HR.

This standardized pre-spinal baseline will be used for assessment of haemodynamic changes during the study.

Spinal anaesthesia will be performed with the patient in the sitting position at the L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace using a 27-G Whitacre needle.

After free flow of cerebrospinal fluid has been established, 12.5 mg hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.5% with fentanyl 25 µg will be injected over approximately 10-15 seconds.

Immediately following the spinal injection, the patient will be positioned supine with approximately 15° left uterine displacement.

No routine fluid preload will be administered. Ringer's acetate solution will be administered at a minimal rate required to maintain intravenous access, with a maximum volume of 500 mL .

Haemodynamic measurements SBP and HR will be recorded at 1-minute intervals from the administration of spinal anaesthesia until delivery.

After delivery, measurements will be obtained at 2-minute intervals until completion of surgery.

The following variables will be recorded:

Baseline SBP and HR. Lowest SBP
interventions: continuous infusion of noreadrenaline at a fixed rate of 30 ml/min of 4ug/ml
continious ephedrine infusion at a rate of 30 ml/min
Patients will receive a combined infusion of norepinephrine 2 µg/min and ephedrine 2 mg/min.
primary_outcomes: The incidence of maternal hypotension from initiation of spinal anaesthesia until end of the opertation .
title: Comparison of Prophylactic Continuous Infusion of Norepinephrine, Ephedrine, and Their Combination for Prevention of Hypotension During Spinal Anaesthesia for Caesarean Delivery

The investigators aim to confirm pilot study findings (REB 119638) on the effects of delayed release apple cider vinegar (drACV). Our pilot study recruited 11 participants from the First Episode Mood and Anxiety Program (FEMAP) who had experienced (by self-report) weight gain concurrent with medication use. The investigators found that drACV was well tolerated with adherence above 90% and resulted in reduced LDL cholesterol, improved lipids in 7 participants, altered microbiota composition in the direction associated with improved metabolic and mental health outcomes, and the emergence of a potential "responder phenotype". The investigators did not, however, find significant effects on weight.

The investigators aim to expand that study by 1) including a larger sample; 2) Conducting a detailed analysis of the microbiome and identifying immune and genomic factors associated with response, thereby further defining responder and non-responder phenotypes that emerged in the initial analysis, 3) collecting additional biological, psychological, and social data to permit complex multivariate modelling on gene-environment interactions for mechanistic research.

The investigators will seek to recruit sixty-two participants from FEMAP, the General Adult Ambulatory Mental Health Services (GAAMHS) and Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services at LHSC. Participants need to have experienced weight gain by self-report and clinician estimation, be psychiatrically stable on steady doses of medication, and be between the ages of 16-45.

After leukapheresis for CAR-T cell manufacture, participants receive lymphodepleting conditioning (fludarabine 30 mg/m\^2/day plus cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m\^2/day on Days -5 to -3), followed by a single intravenous infusion of CLL-1-CD70 CAR-T cells. Dose escalation follows a traditional 3+3 design with planned dose levels of 0.5 x 10\^6, 1 x 10\^6, and 2 x 10\^6 CAR-T cells/kg, guided by dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) assessed during Days 1-28 after infusion. The primary endpoint is safety and tolerability, as assessed by treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), including cytokine release syndrome (CRS), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), hematologic toxicity, organ toxicity, infections, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis/macrophage activation syndrome (HLH/MAS), and tumor lysis syndrome (TLS). Efficacy will be evaluated by the composite complete remission rate (CRc, defined as the proportion of patients achieving CR, CRh, or CRi) at prespecified time points according to the European LeukemiaNet (ELN) 2022 criteria, overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), duration of response (DOR), and cumulative incidence of relapse (CIR) over a 1-year follow-up period. Immune reconstitution following CAR-T cell infusion will also be assessed at prespecified time points. CAR-T cellular kinetics in peripheral blood (CAR transgene copies, Cmax, Tmax, and AUC0-28d) will also be evaluated.

brief_summary:
Elderly patients on direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), specifically factor Xa (FXa) inhibitors such as apixaban and rivaroxaban are at elevated risk of haematoma expansion following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Andexanet alfa is a recombinant modified factor Xa decoy protein that directly reverses the anticoagulant effect of FXa inhibitors. The pivotal ANNEXA-4 single-arm trial reported hemostatic efficacy of approximately 82% in the overall cohort and 82.9% among patients with intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). The subsequent ANNEXA-I randomised controlled trial demonstrated 67.0% hemostatic efficacy with andexanet alfa compared with 53.1% in the usual-care group (adjusted difference 13.4 percentage points; p=0.003) among patients with spontaneous ICH. However, both landmark trials were focused predominantly on spontaneous ICH, and TBI-specific real-world data on andexanet alfa remain limited.

This retrospective single-centre cohort study evaluates the hemostatic efficacy and safety of andexanet alfa in adult patients with traumatic intracranial haemorrhage who were received FXa inhibitor anticoagulation. All patients had a baseline computed tomography (CT) scan and at least one follow-up CT within 24 hours of andexanet alfa administration. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients achieving excellent or good hemostatic efficacy, defined by the percentage change in haematoma volume (for intraparenchymal haemorrhage, IPH) or maximum thickness (for subdural haematoma, SDH; epidural haematoma, EDH; or subarachnoid haemorrhage, SAH) between baseline and follow-up CT: Excellent (≤20% increase), Good (21-35% increase), or Poor (\>35% increase). Key secondary outcomes include 30-day all-cause mortality, thrombotic complications (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction), reduction in anti-factor Xa activity, neurosurgical intervention rate, and hospital and ICU length of stay.
primary_outcomes: Hemostatic Efficacy
title: Andexanet Alfa for Reversal of Factor Xa Inhibitors in Traumatic Brain Injury: A Retrospective Single-Centre Study

brief_summary:

However, an effective screening program requires not only collecting a screening test, but also ensuring seamless continuity across the entire care pathway, including adequate specimen collection, accurate laboratory reporting, prompt referral, timely colposcopy, biopsy confirmation, treatment, and follow-up. Delays or breakdowns at any stage can increase the risk of disease progression.

This prospective observational clinical audit aims to evaluate the quality, timeliness, and continuity of cervical cytology services at the Early Cancer Detection Unit, Women's Health Hospital, Assiut University.

Women attending the unit who are eligible for cervical screening will be invited to participate. Because this is an observational audit of standard healthcare services, all examinations, tests, and treatments (such as Pap smears, colposcopies, cervical biopsies, and excisional or ablative therapies) are performed strictly according to routine clinical indications and standard management guidelines. No experimental interventions or tests will be administered.

The study will prospectively monitor participants along the clinical pathway to evaluate:

* The rate of adequate Pap smear specimens and distribution of cytological findings.
* Time intervals between screening, cytology results, specialty referral, colposcopy examination, histopathological diagnosis, and definitive treatment.
* Rates of completed referrals, colposcopy appointments, biopsy confirmations, and definitive treatments.
* Reasons for delayed appointments, missed visits, or loss to follow-up through clinical record reviews and routine patient contact.

The findings will help identify patient, provider, and health-system factors contributing to care gaps, providing evidence-based quality indicators to enhance the efficiency and clinical performance of cervical screening services.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Cervical Cytology Specimen Adequacy
title: Clinical Audit of Cervical Cytology Services in an Early Cancer Detection Unit

brief_summary:
Overweight and obesity are common metabolic disorders associated with increased risks of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and other health problems. The gut microbiota plays an important role in regulating metabolism, inflammation, and intestinal health. Akkermansia, a beneficial gut bacterium, has been associated with metabolic health and may have potential benefits for weight management.

This study aims to investigate the relationship between gut microbiota characteristics and overweight or obesity and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Akkermansia supplementation in individuals with overweight or obesity.

The study consists of two stages. The first stage is an observational study comparing gut microbiota characteristics between healthy individuals and individuals with overweight or obesity. The second stage is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in which eligible participants with overweight or obesity will receive either Akkermansia supplementation or placebo once daily for 12 weeks, followed by follow-up through Week 24.

The study will evaluate changes in body weight, metabolic health, gut microbiota characteristics, related metabolites, and safety outcomes. The findings may provide clinical evidence regarding the potential use of Akkermansia supplementation for the management of overweight and obesity.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Body Weight from Baseline at Week 12
title: Gut Microbiota-Based Clinical Study of Akkermansia Supplementation for Overweight and Obesity

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does postoperative bupivacaine infusion through a perineural catheter reduce intravenous opioid consumption within the first 48 hours after surgery compared with intravenous opioid analgesia alone?
* Does the postoperative Bupivacaine infusion through perineural catheter help in reducing the phantom pain at 6 months follow-up?
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain

brief_summary:
Vitiligo is a common, long-lasting disease that happens when the immune system attacks melanocytes (skin cells that produce the skin-coloring pigment melanin) in the skin leading to loss of color. Non-segmental vitiligo (NSV) occurs when patches of color loss appear on both sides of the body, such as both knees or both hands. This study is to evaluate how effective, safe and tolerable upadacitinib is for the treatment of non-segmental vitiligo in pediatric participants ages 6 to 11 years old.

This study will have two periods: Period A and Period B. In Period A, participants are placed in 1 of 2 groups called treatment arms. Each group receives a different treatment. There is a 1 in 2 chance that participants will receive placebo. Participants who complete Period A will continue into Period B and remain on blinded treatment.

In Studies 1 and 2: Period A, participants will receive oral tablets (or oral solution) of upadacitinib or placebo once a day for 48 weeks. In Period B,participants who complete Period A will continue into Period B and remain on blinded treatment for 112 weeks. Participants will be followed up for 30 days. This study will enroll approximately 154 pediatric participants at 110 sites worldwide.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care (due to study procedures). Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic. The effect of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving Facial-Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI) 75 (>= 75% Improvement in F-VASI From Baseline)
Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Study to Learn How Effective, Safe, and Tolerable Upadacitinib is for Young Participants With Non-segmental Vitiligo

brief_summary:
Ticks in Finland can carry several microbes that may infect humans. The best known tick-borne diseases are Lyme borreliosis and tick-borne encephalitis (TBE). In recent years, scientists have also found other microbes in Finnish ticks, such as Anaplasma, Rickettsia, Neoehrlichia, Borrelia miyamotoi, and Babesia. Infections caused by these microbes are called emerging tick-borne diseases. Climate change may also increase the number of ticks and expand their range further north. This could lead to more tick-borne diseases in the future.

The public health impact of these emerging infections is still unclear. Some of them may cause severe illness, especially in people with weakened immune systems or without a spleen. However, we still know little about how common these infections are, how they develop in the body, and what symptoms they cause. Some people may have no symptoms, while others may become seriously ill. Good diagnostic tests are also lacking.

More knowledge is also needed about Lyme borreliosis and TBE. Some forms of Lyme disease, such as arthritis, heart inflammation, or eye problems, may be underdiagnosed. In addition, TBE cases have increased in Finland in recent years. This study will examine the symptoms, recovery, and quality of life of patients with these infections.

Another goal is to improve laboratory diagnostics. Current tests for Lyme disease and TBE mainly detect antibodies. These tests cannot always tell when the infection occurred or distinguish a past Lyme borreliosis infection from a current one. This also makes it difficult to detect reinfections in Lyme borreliosis or TBE-infections in vaccinated individuals. By collecting samples from patients, we aim to develop better diagnostic methods.

The main goal of the study is to improve knowledge about tick-borne diseases in Finland. We will study how common emerging infections are, what symptoms they cause, and whether people can have more than one tick-borne infection at the same time. We will also examine how the immune system responds to these infections and how this relates to disease severity and recovery.

This study includes both children and adults who are being examined for a suspected tick-borne disease. Participants will be followed for six months using questionnaires at initiation, one, three, and six months. Blood samples and other samples, depending on the patient's symptoms, will be collected together with routine clinical samples. The samples will be analyzed to detect tick-borne pathogens and antibodies against them. Molecular tests (PCR) will look for the genetic material of the microbes. Researchers will also search for new biological markers of these diseases and study the immune response using advanced laboratory methods.

The study will be conducted in collaboration with the SWETICK study.
primary_outcomes: The number of diagnosed neoehrlichiosis cases
The number of diagnosed cases with Borrelia miyamotoi -infection
The number of diagnosed babesiosis cases
The number of diagnosed anaplasmosis cases
The number of diagnosed rickettsiosis cases
The number of diagnosed Lyme borreliosis cases
The number of diagnosed tick-borne encephalitis cases
title: FINtick - a Prospective Multicenter Study on Tick-borne Infections in Finland

brief_summary:
Severe Alcohol-associated hepatitis, is associated with significant morbidity and mortality.1,2 Of the various treatment modalities evaluated for treatment of Severe Alcoholic hepatitis, corticosteroids have been the most extensively studied.1 Five out of 13 randomized controlled trials, and four out of 5 meta-analysis have shown a survival benefit with corticosteroids, especially in patients with DF ≥32 and/ or encephalopathy.1-4 However, the role of corticosteroidsin Severe Alcoholic hepatitis still remains controversial.5-6Corticosteroid therapy is not considered the ideal option by mostauthors because their beneficial effect seems to be confined to a highly select minority group in which the inhibitory effect of corticosteroids on liverinflammation is not outweighed by side effects such as weakened defence against infections, anti-anabolic effects, and possible ulcer promoting effects.6Corticosteroids are usually contraindicated in those with DF \> 54 or MELD \>247 .Also corticosteroidsare contraindicated in those with renal failure, gastro-intestinal bleed, pancreatitis and active sepsis. Therefore, there have been constant efforts to evaluate new therapies for Severe Alcoholic hepatitis (SAH). In a recent trial, combination of glucocorticoids plus N-acetylcysteine was found to improve one month survival in patients with Severe Alcoholic hepatitis, compared with glucocorticoids alone. However, the 6 month survival similar in both the groups.8 Human colostrum and bovine colostrum are rich in protein, immunoglobulin, lactoferrin and growth factors. Recent studies suggest that colostrum components, immunoglobulin and growth factor benefits physically active personas well as in the treatment of autoimmune disorders. It is used for the treatment of a wide variety of gastrointestinal conditions, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatorydrug-induced gut injury, Helicobacter pylori infection, immune deficiency related diarrhea as well as infective diarrhea.9,10,11It has also been sucessfully used to significantly decrease the level of Endotoxemia - lower levels of Lipopolysaccharides.

We plan to compare the efficacy of bovine colostrum versus Placebo (Pasteurized milk powder) alone in treatment of severe alcoholic hepatitis.
primary_outcomes: Survival at 3 month
title: Bovine Colostrum In The Treatment Of Severe Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis

This study will include participants who have already undergone ESR1 testing as part of their standard medical care. Patient real-world data will be extracted by the patient's medical records. No additional procedures or visits beyond routine care will be required. Data will be collected from routine clinical visits and standard-of-care treatment.

title: ESR1 Mutations in Metastatic Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer in the Greek Population

brief_summary: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition in which infection triggers widespread inflammation and blood clotting abnormalities. Many patients with sepsis develop coagulopathy (impaired blood clotting), which contributes to organ damage and death. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius L.) is a traditional Chinese medicine herb with documented anticoagulant, anti-platelet, and blood vessel-protective properties. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial will enroll 210 adult patients with sepsis-associated coagulopathy at Ruijin Hospital. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: high-dose safflower granules (equivalent to 9 g of raw herb daily), medium-dose safflower granules (equivalent to 6 g of raw herb daily), matching placebo (equivalent to 0.6 g of raw herb daily for blinding). The granules are dissolved in 50 mL of warm water and given through a nasogastric tube once daily for 7 days, in addition to standard sepsis treatment. The primary outcome is the improvement in the SOFA score (a measure of organ function) at 14 days. Secondary outcomes include DIC scores, coagulation tests, endothelial injury and platelet markers, inflammatory markers, 28-day mortality, length of ICU and hospital stay, and adverse events. The study is funded by Ruijin Hospital as an investigator-initiated trial.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in SOFA score from baseline to Day 14
title: Safflower (Carthamus Tinctorius L.) Granules for Sepsis-associated Coagulopathy

brief_summary:
This study compares shock wave therapy with high-intensity laser therapy for tailbone pain, also called coccydynia. It includes adults aged 18 to 65 years who have had tailbone pain for at least 3 months and continue to have symptoms despite previous standard treatments.

The main question is whether the two treatments differ in how much they reduce tailbone pain while sitting. The main comparison will be between pain before treatment and pain 3 months after the final treatment session. The study will also examine earlier pain relief, daily activities, and sitting ability.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two treatment groups. One group will receive 6 shock wave therapy sessions, with 2 sessions per week. The other group will receive 10 high-intensity laser therapy sessions, with 3 sessions per week. Both treatments will be applied to the tailbone area by an experienced physician.

Participants will be assessed before the first treatment session and 1 and 3 months after the final treatment session. They will rate their overall tailbone pain and pain while sitting on scales from 0 to 10. They will also complete questionnaires about how pain affects daily activities. At follow-up visits, participants will report changes in their condition and satisfaction with treatment.

The study will also record sitting duration, the ability to sit for 30 minutes, pain medicine use, the need for additional treatment, and any unwanted symptoms or medical problems.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Sitting-Related Coccygeal Pain on the Numeric Rating Scale at 3 Months After Treatment Completion
title: Shock Wave Therapy Versus High-Intensity Laser Therapy for Coccydynia (Tailbone Pain)

brief_summary:
Stroke can occur when a blood clot travels to the brain and blocks blood flow. In some patients, these blood clots may originate in the heart. Standard emergency stroke imaging typically includes a CT scan of the head and CT angiography (CTA) of the head and neck, but does not routinely include imaging of the heart.

This study will evaluate whether cardiac CT angiography (CTA) can be safely added to the standard acute stroke imaging workflow without delaying urgent stroke care. Participants with suspected acute ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA) will undergo either prospective ECG-gated cardiac CTA or non-ECG-gated cardiac CTA during their acute stroke imaging examination.

The primary goal of the study is to assess the feasibility of integrating cardiac CTA into routine stroke imaging by evaluating workflow impact, image quality, radiation exposure, contrast use, and protocol completion. Findings from this study may help improve the identification of cardiac sources of stroke and inform the design of future larger studies.

brief_summary:
National Highly Specialized Care (NHV) is provided in Sweden to children and adolescents with severe and treatment-resistant self-harm or eating disorders when previous treatment has not led to sufficient improvement. NHV offers intensive, individualized care delivered by multidisciplinary teams with specialized expertise.

This observational study aims to evaluate NHV provided at two specialized psychiatric services in Region Stockholm: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Stockholm (BUP Stockholm), for severe self-harm, and the Stockholm Centre for Eating Disorders (SCÄ), for children with severe eating disorders.

The primary aim is to explore patients' and their parents' or legal guardians' experiences of NHV and their perceptions of its effects through qualitative interviews conducted at treatment completion and one year later.

Secondary aims are to evaluate treatment feasibility, adherence, and changes in psychiatric symptoms, functioning, and skills during and after treatment. Data are collected through questionnaires completed by patients and their parents or legal guardians, clinical assessments, and medical records.

Assessments are conducted 1) at baseline, which is defined as the first treatment week, 2) after six weeks of treatment, 3) at regular treatment completion (approximately 12-13 weeks), 4) if the treatment is extended by 4-6 weeks due to, for example, severe comorbidity, an additional assessment is conducted at the end of this treatment extension, 5) at six-month follow-up, and 6) at twelve-month follow-up after treatment completion.

The study aims to improve understanding of the benefits and limitations of NHV and contribute to the further development of specialized psychiatric care for children and adolescents with complex treatment needs.

Treatment Completion Rate
Treatment Attendance

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, open-label, superiority randomized controlled trial enrolling adult patients aged 18 to 75 years. All participants have abdominal obesity (BMI ≥ 28 kg/m² with specific waist circumference standards) and non-valvular atrial fibrillation, and have successfully regained normal heart rhythm after their first catheter ablation.

The study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of weekly mazdutide injection with conventional routine care in preventing heart rhythm recurrence within 12 months after ablation (excluding a 3-month early recovery blanking period). A total of 24 months will be spent recruiting participants, followed by a 12-month follow-up period.

Participants are randomly divided into two groups. The intervention group receives escalating-dose mazdutide subcutaneous injections starting within 48 hours after ablation alongside standard health guidance on diet, exercise and lifestyle. The control group only receives the same routine health guidance without mazdutide treatment.

The primary efficacy endpoint is recurrence of atrial arrhythmias (including AF, atrial flutter, and atrial tachycardia) recorded on a standard 12-lead surface ECG for ≥10 seconds, or on a 24-hour Holter monitor (including single-lead ECG patches) for \>30 seconds, at 12 months after a single ablation procedure (after a 3-month blanking period), without the use of any Class I/III antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs).
primary_outcomes: Recurrence of atrial arrhythmias at 12 months after a single ablation procedure without the use of any Class I/III antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs).
Composite serious adverse events (SAEs) occurring during the perioperative period and follow-up period.
title: Mazdutide for Reducing Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation in Obese Patients

brief_summary:
This study investigates whether temporarily blocking the ghrelin receptor affects appetite and food intake in people with overweight or obesity. Ghrelin is a hormone that stimulates hunger; the researchers are using LEAP2, a naturally occurring hormone that blocks ghrelin's receptor, as a research tool to study what happens when ghrelin signaling is turned off for 24 hours.

The study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Eighteen adults with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥25 kg/m², elevated body fat percentage) will each complete two 24-hour study visits, at least 7 days apart: one with a continuous LEAP2 infusion and one with a saline placebo infusion, in random order. Neither participants nor most study staff will know which treatment is given on which visit.

During each 24-hour visit, participants will receive a standardized liquid test meal followed by ad libitum (eat-until-comfortably-full) lunch, dinner, and breakfast meals, plus access to snacks. The main question the study aims to answer is whether LEAP2 reduces the total amount of food eaten over 24 hours compared to placebo. Additional measurements include blood glucose levels, subjective feelings of hunger and fullness (via questionnaires), stomach emptying rate, blood pressure and heart rate, and hormone levels (including growth hormone, FSH, and LH). Some participants will also undergo a small fat tissue biopsy to study how genes and proteins related to metabolism respond.

The results are expected to improve understanding of how ghrelin and LEAP2 regulate appetite and metabolism in people with obesity, which may inform future approaches to treating obesity and related metabolic conditions.
primary_outcomes: Food intake
title: Investigating the Effects of 24 Hour LEAP2 Infusion in Individuals With Overweight and Obesity

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, single-arm phase 2 clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and clinical applicability of Middle Segmental Gastrectomy (MSG) for patients with gastric cancer

* MSG is a function-preserving surgical technique that resects the middle portion of the stomach while preserving the pylorus and the upper stomach (cardia and fundus) to minimize common postoperative issues such as dumping syndrome and nutritional deficiencies

The primary objective of the study is to determine the incidence of dumping syndrome at 1 year postoperatively (defined as a Sigstad score ≥ 7) and evaluate if it differs significantly from the 15.8% incidence reported for standard laparoscopic distal gastrectomy (LDG) in the KLASS 04 study . The study targets adult patients with mid- or high-body gastric adenocarcinoma with a tumor size of 4 cm or less at clinical stages cT1N0/1M0 or cT2N0/1M0 (well or moderately differentiated)

. Secondary evaluations include monitoring postoperative reflux symptoms, changes in nutritional indicators (such as weight and hemoglobin), quality of life (QOL) using EORTC QLQ-C30 and STO22, and 3-year recurrence-free and overall survival rates.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Dumping Syndrome at 1 Year Postoperatively (Sigstad Score ≥7)
title: Feasibility Study of Middle Segmental Gastrectomy (MSG) for Gastric Cancer.

brief_summary:
Thirteen types of EDS have been described based on their clinical manifestations and genetic backgrounds. Their diagnosis relies on personal and family medical history, together with established clinical criteria. A definitive diagnosis can then be confirmed through genetic testing. However, definitive diagnosis of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS), the most common EDS subtype (\>80% of cases), remains impossible because its molecular basis is still unknown.

The diagnosis of hEDS is based on a set of clinical criteria, some of which are subject to examiner interpretation. These criteria have limitations at the extremes of age and in mild or incomplete forms, potentially preventing a formal diagnosis. Patients may consequently experience a diagnostic odyssey and psychological distress, without recognition of their condition or access to appropriate management.

The diagnosis of hEDS is further complicated by the overlap between its clinical manifestations and those of Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders (HSD), which are relatively common in the general population (1-3%). HSD are also characterized by joint hypermobility, which may be complicated by joint instability and pain, but unlike hEDS, they are not associated with tissue fragility. There is therefore an urgent need to identify a reliable, simple, reproducible, and widely accessible diagnostic criterion to establish a diagnosis of hEDS in the large population of hypermobile patients.

Tenascin-X (TN-X) is a glycoprotein involved in the assembly of the ECM. One study showed that TN-X levels were reduced by 35% in 52% of hypermobile patients (9/17) compared with healthy controls. This finding suggests a possible association between serum TN-X levels and hEDS. However, no correlation has yet been investigated.

We hypothesize that serum TN-X levels could serve as a biological diagnostic criterion for hEDS.
primary_outcomes: Measurement of TN-X concentration
title: Evaluation of the Role of Serum Tenascin-X Levels in the Diagnosis of Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

brief_summary:
Study Background \& Purpose:

The no-reflow phenomenon is a significant complication occurring in patients with acute myocardial infarction who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). It leads to poor myocardial perfusion despite successful opening of the culprit coronary artery. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have demonstrated cardioprotective mechanisms beyond glucose control.

Objective:

This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of administering SGLT2 inhibitors as adjunctive therapy in reducing the incidence of the no-reflow phenomenon in patients with myocardial infarction undergoing PCI.

Study Plan:

Eligible patients presenting with myocardial infarction scheduled for PCI will be randomized into three groups: one group receiving standard pharmacological care plus Empagliflozin therapy, second group receiving standard pharmacological care plus dapagliflozin therapy, and the control group receiving standard pharmacological care alone. Patients will be monitored during and after the procedure to evaluate coronary blood flow and incidence of no reflow phenomenon.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of angiographic no-reflow/impaired myocardial reperfusion
title: Evaluating SGLT2 Inhibitors for the Reduction of No-Reflow Phenomenon in Patients Undergoing PCI

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate if a 3D face scanner is a reliable and accurate tool for measuring the vertical dimension of occlusion (the optimal height of the lower face) in patients who have lost all their teeth.

Currently, dentists determine this measurement manually using clinical judgment, which can sometimes lead to inconsistent results. This study will compare the traditional manual measurement method with a digital face scanning technique.

Eighteen completely edentulous (toothless) participants will be enrolled. Each participant will receive two sets of complete dentures: one set fabricated using the new digital face scanning technique and one set fabricated using the traditional method. Researchers will take facial measurements using both a digital caliper directly on the patient's face and a software tool on the 3D scans. The results will help determine if digital scanning is a dependable alternative to conventional methods for improving denture fit, function, and patient comfort.
primary_outcomes: Accuracy digital face scan in vertical Dimension of Occlusion Measurements
title: Comparison of Conventional and Face Scan in Recording the Vertical Dimension of Completely Edentulous Patients

brief_summary: This retrospective study aims to investigate whether a specific substance in the blood, called Sphingosine-1-Phosphate (S1P), is related to the degree of osseointegration around dental implants. We will review the medical records of 20 patients who have already completed their dental implant surgery and standard follow-up. The S1P levels will be measured using leftover blood samples from their routine preoperative examinations. By analyzing their existing dental x-ray images (CBCT) taken before surgery and during their routine 3-month follow-up, we will evaluate the osseointegration and implant stability. Ultimately, we hope to find out if measuring S1P levels from routine blood tests can help predict the quality of osseointegration after getting dental implants.
primary_outcomes: Correlation between serum S1P levels and dental implant osseointegration

brief_summary:
Boxing is a combat sport that requires repetitive, high-speed upper extremity movements, placing substantial demands on shoulder stability, scapular control, and neuromuscular coordination. Repetitive punching movements may contribute to scapular dyskinesis, shoulder dysfunction, and impaired upper extremity performance. Scapular stabilization exercises aim to improve scapular positioning, muscle activation, and movement coordination by targeting key stabilizing muscles, including the serratus anterior and trapezius.

The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of scapular stabilization exercises on scapular control and upper extremity performance in adolescent boxers. Scapular control, muscular endurance, stability, strength, balance, and reaction time will be assessed to determine changes following the exercise intervention. The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the potential benefits of scapular stabilization training for improving upper extremity function and sports performance in adolescent boxers.
primary_outcomes: Scapular Dyskinesis
Lateral Scapular Slide Test
title: Effects of Scapular Training on Adolescent Boxers

brief_summary:
Adipose tissue is with endocrine properties and secretes many cytokines. Some of these cytokines are concerned with ischemic heart disease. I hypothesized that significant surgical reduction in adipose tissue mass leads to decrease in its cell population which may pose significantly reduced production of adipokines ( Leptin and Angiotensin) associated with ischemic heart disease in obese people.

Study objectives are analysis of Leptin, Angiotensin-II, mRNA expression analysis of leptin, leptin receptor and Angiotensin-II. investigation of genetic variations in the Leptin, Leptin receptors, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors, confirm SNPs of selected sample. Ddetermination of the association of genetic variation in Leptin receptor, angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors with Leptin and Angiotensin-II levels and determination of effect of genetic variation on the transcriptional regulation.

Case control study having 212 patients (106 patients in each group) with type I Obese adults, both males and pre-menopausal females belonging to ASA 1 and 2 requiring stagged liposuction will be included. Exclusion of subjects with Diabetes mellitus, Metabolic syndrome, Endocrine disorders, on statin drugs, not willing to participate.

After informed consent, blood samples will be taken to quantify plasma levels of Leptin and Angiotensin II pre-operatively by ELISA.

DNA will also be extracted from blood and SNPs will be analysed. The selected SNPs will be amplified by PCR and product will be purified and analysed by agarose gel electrophoresis.

Patients will undergo liposuction and RNA will be isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue for reverse transcription.

After 3 months, patients will be called back for second session of liposuction and plasma level of Leptin and Angiotensin II will be quantified again. Similarly, expression profile of transcription factors will also be analysed again. Paired t-test will be used to compare clinical parameters like serum adipokines levels and adipokines expression levels and p value \<0.05 will be taken as statistically significant. The results will be utilized to determine impact of surgical reduction on plasma level and expression of the adipokines in minimizing cardiovascular risk factors.
primary_outcomes: plasma level and expression of the adipokines
title: Impact of Significant Surgical Reduction of Adipose Tissue on Plasma Levels and Genetic Expression of Adipokines Associated With Ischemic Heart Disease in Type I Obesity.
