brief_summary: The objective of this study is to provide a regional, mechanistic characterization of pulmonary ventilation changes following treatment with the Apreo BREATHE System, using hyperpolarized ¹²⁹Xe MRI, in BREATHE-3 participants. BREATHE-Xe is designed to generate mechanistic signals regarding whether airway scaffolds reduce ventilation defects, improve gas exchange, and correlate with CT and spirometric/plethysmographic changes observed in BREATHE-3. Findings support mechanistic interpretation and future hypothesis generation.
primary_outcomes: Primary Endpoint
title: Xenon MRI to Evaluate Changes to Lung Function Following Bronchoscopic Treatment of Air Trapping in Emphysema

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether breathing effort and patient-ventilator asynchrony (PVA) during the transition phase are associated with clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated adults.The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the level and change in breathing effort associated with successful liberation from mechanical ventilation?
* How often does PVA occur during the transition phase?
* Are breathing effort and PVA associated with patient outcomes?

These questions will be assessed using physiological and clinical data collected during the transition phase of mechanical ventilation. Breathing effort will be measured twice daily using a non-invasive airway pressure measurement, while ventilator waveforms will be continuously monitored to detect PVA. Participants will be followed up at day 28 and day 90.
primary_outcomes: Successful liberation from mechanical ventilation within 28 days of enrollment
title: Impact of Inspiratory Effort and Patient-Ventilator Interaction During the Transition Phase

brief_summary:
Osteoporosis represents a major public health concern, particularly among older adults, due to its association with an increased risk of fragility fractures, functional limitations, and loss of independence. According to current clinical guidelines, bone-specific pharmacological therapies represent a cornerstone of fracture prevention in individuals at increased fracture risk. Although these treatments effectively improve bone mineral density and reduce osteoporotic fractures, their effects on fall-related risk factors, including muscle weakness, impaired balance, reduced mobility, and fall frequency, are limited. Importantly, osteoporotic fractures result from the interaction of reduced bone strength and increased fall risk, emphasizing the need for preventive strategies that address both determinants.

Physical exercise therefore represents an essential component of comprehensive osteoporosis management. In addition to its beneficial effects on bone strength, appropriately designed exercise programs can improve muscle strength, balance, and functional performance, thereby reducing the risk of falls. Accordingly, the recently published German S3 guideline "Physical Exercise for Fracture Prevention" (2025) recommends risk-adapted exercise interventions that simultaneously address skeletal and neuromuscular determinants of osteoporotic fractures. An important feature of this guideline is the differentiation of individuals according to their bone status, fall risk, and functional capacity, allowing specific training objectives and exercise recommendations to be assigned to different fracture risk groups.

Despite these recommendations, the availability of guideline-based, osteoporosis-specific exercise programs in routine healthcare remains limited. Existing supervised exercise programs are not universally accessible and frequently require qualified instructors, suitable facilities, and regular attendance at predefined times. These requirements may represent substantial barriers, particularly for older individuals with impaired mobility, limited access to exercise facilities, or difficulties attending scheduled exercise sessions. Furthermore, the availability of supervised exercise programs varies considerably between regions, potentially contributing to inequalities in osteoporosis care.

Home-based exercise programs may overcome these limitations by providing a flexible, accessible, and cost-effective alternative that can be performed independently of location and without continuous supervision. Such programs may be particularly attractive to older individuals who prefer exercising independently in their familiar home environment. However, currently available home-based exercise programs for individuals with osteoporosis are rarely based on comprehensive, risk-specific exercise guidelines. Furthermore, their effectiveness in improving relevant determinants of osteoporotic fracture risk has not been adequately evaluated in controlled clinical studies.

To address this gap, a series of structured, guideline-based home exercise programs was developed based on the recommendations of the German S3 guideline "Physical Exercise for Fracture Prevention". These programs specifically consider different combinations of reduced bone strength, fall risk, and functional limitations, allowing exercise selection and training objectives to be adapted to the individual's fracture risk profile. The development process included the selection of appropriate exercises, their integration into structured training programs, and the preparation of visual instructions to facilitate independent and safe exercise performance in the home environment.

The present study focuses on individuals characterized by substantially reduced bone strength (osteoporosis), relevant fall risk factors, but no previous osteoporotic fractures. This population represents an important target group for preventive interventions, as both major determinants of fracture risk are present, while physical exercise may still offer considerable potential to improve neuromuscular function and maintain mobility and independence.

The primary purpose of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a newly developed, guideline-based home exercise program in individuals with osteoporosis and increased fall risk. Specifically, the study aims to determine whether the intervention favorably affects surrogate measures of bone strength, fall risk, and functional mobility. The central research question is whether a structured, independently performed, risk-adapted home exercise program can improve these key determinants of osteoporotic fracture risk and thereby provide an effective, accessible, and practical exercise-based strategy for fracture prevention in this high-risk population.

By evaluating this intervention, the study aims to contribute to the implementation of evidence-based exercise recommendations in routine osteoporosis care and to establish a scientific basis for the
primary_outcomes: Changes of chair rise test performance
Changes in static balance performance
title: Exercise and Fall Prevention

brief_summary:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a condition in which the immune system damages the brain and spinal cord. Treatments called disease-modifying therapies can reduce inflammation and disease activity. For some people with highly active MS, autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT) may be used. AHSCT uses a person's own blood-forming stem cells after treatment that suppresses the immune system.

REAL-MS is an observational study that will collect and analyse information from routine clinical care to compare the longer-term effectiveness and safety of AHSCT with high-efficacy disease-modifying therapies for adults with MS. High-efficacy therapies include medicines such as alemtuzumab, cladribine, natalizumab, and anti-CD20 antibody treatments, as well as other high-efficacy disease-modifying therapies that may become available during the study.
primary_outcomes: No Evidence of Disease Activity (NEDA-3)
title: REAL-MS: Observational Database Study of AHSCT and MS Therapies

brief_summary:
Epithelial ovarian cancer, which includes fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer, is the deadliest gynecologic malignant neoplasm. The goal of this observational study is to collect real-world data on treatment patterns, clinical effectiveness, participant characteristics, biomarker testing, and health-related quality of life in participants with FRα-positive platinum-resistant ovarian, fallopian tube, and peritoneal cancer receiving mirvetuximab soravtansine.

Mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) is an approved antibody-drug conjugate being studied for the treatment of FRα-positive platinum-resistant ovarian, fallopian tube, and peritoneal cancer. Adult participants with FRα-positive platinum-resistant cancer who have received 1-3 prior treatment lines and are scheduled to receive MIRV as monotherapy will be enrolled. Approximately 500 participants will be enrolled at sites globally.

Participants will receive intravenous infusions of mirvetuximab soravtansine as monotherapy according to the local product label and treating physician's decision. The total study duration per participant may be up to 18 months of follow-up.

There is expected to be no additional burden for participants in this trial. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic according to their routine clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Treatment Duration of MIRV Among Participants With Platinum-Resistant FRα-Positive Ovarian Cancer
title: Real-World Study of Mirvetuximab Soravtansine in Adult Participants With Platinum-Resistant FRα-Positive Ovarian, Fallopian Tube, and Peritoneal Cancer

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, open-label, multicenter, single arm Phase II trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, intracranial efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of MT027 administered ICV in patients with B7-H3-positive brain metastases from advanced solid tumors.

The trial consists of two sequential stages: a safety run-in stage followed by a dose expansion stage. Approximately 40 participants are planned for enrollment, including approximately 3 to 6 participants in the safety run in stage and 34 participants in the dose expansion stage. The final number of participants enrolled may vary depending on the safety findings observed during the safety run-in stage.

Approximately 3 to 6 eligible participants from the primary target population will receive MT027 3×107 CAR+ T cells via ICV injection on Days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. DLTs will be assessed during a 28-day DLT observation period following the first dose.

Following SRC confirmation of acceptable safety during the safety run-in stage, an additional 34 participants will be enrolled to evaluate the intracranial efficacy of MT027 dosed at 3×107 CAR+ T cells.
interventions: Intracerebroventricular injection of MT027 UCAR-T Cell targeting B7H3
primary_outcomes: Incidence rate of Dose-limiting toxicity (DLT)
Intracranial progression-free survival at 6 months (iPFS6)
title: The METAMAX Study: MT027 Allogeneic CAR-T for Brain Metastases From Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
Adolescents and young adults (AYA) with congenital heart disease (CHD) face psychosocial stresses as they transition to adult care. Parents of AYA with CHD also experience increased caregiver burden and psychosocial stresses. Peer support provided by a person with a similar experience has been found to improve disease self-management and psychosocial health outcomes in pediatric healthcare. However, many AYA with CHD still do not have access to formal social support resources. The aim of this study is to improve pediatric to adult transitions in healthcare by evaluating peer mentorship programs for AYA with CHD and their parents.

Established, online mentorship programs, iPeer2Peer(iP2P)/iParent2Parent, will be employed through a pilot feasibility waitlist randomized controlled trial with repeated measures across four sites. Eighty mentees (AYA and parents of AYA) will be recruited and randomized into intervention and control groups. Forty mentees in the intervention group will be matched 1:1 with 30 trained mentors (young adults and parents of AYA). AYA mentees will be matched with young adult mentors and parents of AYA will be matched with other parent mentors. These pairings will connect over 12 weeks through video calls and text messaging to provide peer support to improve self-management and psychosocial health outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Recruitment and withdrawal rates
Adherence
Acceptability/Level of engagement
Barriers/Enablers
title: Optimizing Care Transitions in CHD

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to provide liver stiffness screenings (FibroScans) to patients with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency for the following purposes:

To evaluate the prevalence of elevated liver stiffness among homozygous and heterozygous individuals who carry mutations in the SERPINA1 gene.

To assess whether the coexistence of metabolic or environmental cofactors, such as obesity, diabetes, alcohol use, or hepatic steatosis, modifies the risk of liver fibrosis among those with alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the prevalence of elevated liver stiffness among homozygous and heterozygous individuals who carry mutations in the SERPINA1 gene.
title: AATD-Liver Scan Study

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find better ways to help older adults living in rural areas get access to fresh fruits and vegetables. The researchers want to find out whether delivering fresh produce to the participant's home using a delivery robot is a workable and acceptable way to help them eat more fruits and vegetables.

Participants will:

* Receive fresh fruits and vegetables delivered to their home twice a week by the Robot-Assisted Last-Mile Food Delivery (RALMFD) system; and,
* complete a journal and questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Acceptability of RALMFD
Feasibility of RALMFD
Usability of RALMFD
title: Foodservice Robots Engaging Senior Health

brief_summary: A prospective, multicenter, single-arm clinical study enrolling patients with histologically confirmed invasive carcinoma, clinical stage II-III, known PD-L1 status, and treatment-naïve triple-negative breast cancer. Patients will receive neoadjuvant therapy with pucotenlimab, anlotinib, and nab-paclitaxel, sequentially followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide, for a total of 8 cycles.
primary_outcomes: Total pathological complete response (tpCR) rate
title: Pucotenlimab and Anlotinib in Combination With Chemotherapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how interacting with horses affects autistic children and youth. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How does interacting with horses affect cortisol, heart-rate variability, and electrodermal activity in autistic children and youth?
* How does interacting with horses affect parent-reported behaviors in autistic children and youth? Researchers will compare riding a horse, brushing a horse, and brushing a pretend stuffed horse to see if there are different effects on autistic children's physiology and behavior.

Participants will

* Attend three different horsemanship lessons on three consecutive weeks. One horsemanship lesson will be mounted (riding), one unmounted (brushing), and one with a pretend horse (brushing).
* Wear monitors on their chest and wrist
* Provide saliva samples
primary_outcomes: Electrodermal Activity (EDA)
Heartrate Variability (HRV)
title: Effects of Mounted vs Unmounted Human-Equine Interaction on Autistic Youth

brief_summary:
This Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) investigation aims to further collect evidence on safety and performance of the Mi2000 TICI. This PMCF investigation will prospectively collect clinical data from the use of the Mi2000 TICI and related devices.

This PMCF investigation is performed on a cochlear implant system newly introduced to the market, which was previously studied in two pre-market clinical investigations. The purpose of the current clinical investigation is to collect further evidence by collecting additional clinical data on the use of the Mi2000 TICI.
primary_outcomes: Word Test in Quiet
Sentence Test in Noise
title: Mi2000 TICI - Post-market Implantation Study

brief_summary:
Healthcare systems face persistent challenges in providing coordinated, proactive care for individuals with complex health needs, resulting in high vulnerability to fragmented care, acute clinical deterioration, and frequent emergency hospital admissions. TimelyCare is a proactive, multimodal primary care intervention designed to improve care continuity, optimize hospital-to-home transitions, and reduce unplanned acute healthcare dependency among high-risk individuals. This study evaluates the TimelyCare model using a pragmatic, stepped-wedge matched cluster-controlled trial (SW-CRT) with an open dynamic cohort across 12-15 primary healthcare centers in Region Kalmar, Sweden.

The intervention targets individuals identified through an innovative combined risk algorithm integrating high morbidity (Resource Utilization Bands \[RUB\] levels 4-5) and sociodemographic vulnerability (Demographic Statistical Areas \[DeSO\]). The primary hypothesis is that exposure to the TimelyCare intervention will significantly reduce unplanned hospital admission rates over an 18-month follow-up period compared with usual care, while improving patient-experienced continuity, health-related quality of life, and healthcare cost-effectiveness.
conditions: Primary Care Patients With Chronic Conditions
primary_outcomes: Unplanned Hospital Admission Rate
title: TimelyCare - A Proactive Primary Care Model: Delivering the Right Care at the Right Time for Individuals at Risk of High Care Consumption

brief_summary:
This study is part of the e-Perinatal project and is embedded within the parent e-Perinatal cluster randomized controlled trial (NCT07613008). No additional randomization is performed for this embedded study. Women participating in the parent trial who experience early miscarriage/early pregnancy loss, late miscarriage/second-trimester miscarriage, stillbirth, or neonatal death within the first 28 days of life, together with their participating partners, are eligible for this study.

Participants retain the study-group allocation assigned to their primary healthcare center in the parent trial. Participants from clusters allocated to the intervention arm are offered access to the e-Perinatal Butterfly web-app as a complementary component of the e-Perinatal intervention. The e-Perinatal Butterfly web-app provides tailored psychoeducational resources and digital support tools for parents experiencing perinatal bereavement. Participants from clusters allocated to the control arm continue to receive usual care.

The primary objectives are to assess the feasibility and acceptability of the e-Perinatal Butterfly intervention. The study will also explore changes in symptoms of depression and anxiety among parents who have experienced a perinatal loss. Secondary exploratory analyses will examine longitudinal trajectories of depression and anxiety among bereaved participants and compare these trajectories between the intervention and control arms and with those observed in the broader cohort of the parent e-Perinatal trial
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the intervention
Early acceptability
Final acceptability
title: e-Perinatal Butterfly: An Embedded Study for Parents Experiencing Perinatal Loss

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to investigate whether n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation attenuates abdominal visceral fat accumulation induced by experimental sleep restriction.

Forty healthy adults aged 18-50 years will be randomly assigned to receive n-3 PUFA supplementation (approximately 1.1 g/day of EPA and DHA) or a matching placebo. The intervention will last approximately 75 days, including a 19-day residential sleep protocol consisting of 3 adaptation days, 14 days of sleep restriction (4 hours per night), and 2 recovery days.

The primary outcome is the change in abdominal visceral adipose tissue area measured by CT. Additional assessments include body composition, metabolic and inflammatory markers, gut microbiota, microbial metabolites, and adipose tissue molecular profiles.
primary_outcomes: Change in Visceral Adipose Tissue Area
title: Study on the Mechanism of Central Obesity Induced by Sleep Restriction and the Therapeutic Effect of n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid: a Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Trial (COSPA Study)

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center observational study will enroll 20 adults aged 40 to 75 years with Kellgren-Lawrence grade II or III knee osteoarthritis who have already been scheduled for an intra-articular injection of autologous adipose-derived stromal vascular fraction (SVF) as clinical care. The study does not assign treatment, use a control group, or randomize participants.

After preparation of the therapeutic SVF, residual adipose tissue will be processed independently with a new disposable kit to obtain research-only SVF. No additional adipose tissue will be harvested for research, and research-only SVF will not be injected. Cellular composition and secretome characteristics of research-only SVF will be measured. Synovial fluid biomarkers will be assessed before injection and at 6 months using the same 12-analyte panel. Patient-reported outcomes and knee radiographs will also be compared between baseline and 6 months. CGBio provides research funding and research-only processing kits without involvement in study conduct, analysis, or publication decisions.
interventions: Autologous adipose-derived stromal vascular fraction intra-articular injection
primary_outcomes: Red blood cell contamination of research-only SVF
Total nucleated cell count of research-only SVF
MSC-like stromal progenitor cell composition
CD34-positive adipose stromal progenitor cell composition
Research-only SVF secretome analyte concentrations
Change from baseline in synovial fluid biomarker concentrations at 6 months
title: SVF Cellular Composition, Secretome, and Responses in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies whether different flavored electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) help lower smoking and exposure to tobacco toxicants among cigarette smokers interested in reducing their smoking. ENDS are battery-powered electronic devices designed to deliver a nicotine-containing liquid solution for inhalation. They do not burn tobacco. Previous research has shown that ENDS have the potential to lower exposure to potentially toxic substances compared to burned cigarettes as well as lower short-term adverse health outcomes. However, there are many different ENDS products with varying characteristics, including different flavors, and a need remains to understand more how flavors affect ENDS use, the potential reduction in cigarette use, and exposure to toxicants. This trial studies how two different flavors, fruit and tobacco, affect an individual's smoking behavior and ultimately whether flavored ENDS can help lower smoking and exposure to tobacco toxicants among cigarette smokers interested in reducing their smoking.
primary_outcomes: Change in Cigarettes per day (CPD) from baseline to 12 month follow up visit
Measure Change in biomarker concentration NNAL
title: Flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems to Lower Smoking and Exposure to Tobacco Toxicants Among Cigarette Smokers Interested in Quitting, REFLECT Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this educational study is to learn whether AI smart glasses can score and give feedback on endotracheal intubation performed by medical students on a manikin, and when this AI feedback is most useful during anesthesia training. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do AI scores of the intubation OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination) agree with scores given by faculty examiners?
* Does practicing with AI smart-glasses feedback before or after the airway lecture lead to better intubation OSCE performance, self-efficacy, and cognitive load?

Medical interns rotating through the Department of Anesthesiology at Tri-Service General Hospital (Taiwan) for 2 weeks will be randomized by rotation group to practice intubation once with the AI smart glasses either before the airway lecture (week 1) or after it (week 2). At the end of the rotation, all participants will take an intubation OSCE while wearing the AI glasses, scored independently by a faculty examiner and by the AI. Participants will also complete short questionnaires on self-efficacy (before and after the rotation) and cognitive load (after AI practice). All procedures are performed on a manikin; no patients are involved.
interventions: AI smart-glasses intubation practice with automated feedback
primary_outcomes: Agreement Between AI and Faculty Examiner Total Scores on the Intubation OSCE
title: AI Smart Glasses Feedback for Intubation Training in Medical Students

brief_summary:
This study will compare two approaches to rehabilitation after surgery for a fracture of the upper part of the shinbone that involves the knee joint (tibial plateau fracture). The main question is whether a personalized plan for putting weight on the injured leg, combined with feedback from smart crutch tips, helps patients return to walking without assistance sooner than usual care, without increasing complications.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups:

* Personalized rehabilitation: Researchers will use CT and MRI scans taken after surgery to create a computer model of the repaired bone and estimate how it responds to different loads. The treating doctor will use this information, together with the patient's clinical condition, to prescribe how much weight the patient may place on the injured leg. Smart Crutch Tips will provide feedback to help the patient follow this prescription.
* Usual care: The treating doctor will prescribe weight-bearing according to usual clinical practice. Participants will also use Smart Crutch Tips, but the devices will record information without showing the patient loading data, step counts, or related alerts.

Researchers will compare how long it takes participants to walk independently without crutches, a cane, or another walking aid. They will also assess bone healing, knee function, pain, swelling, fear of movement, adherence to weight-bearing instructions, and complications.

Participants will attend follow-up visits and complete assessments of their recovery. Imaging specialists who do not know which treatment group participants are in will assess fracture healing and whether the repaired bone has remained in position.
primary_outcomes: Time to Sustained Independent Walking Without Walking Aids
title: Personalized Weight-Bearing With Smart Crutch Tips After Surgery for Tibial Plateau Fractures

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to compare two methods for teaching psychiatric work-history interviewing to third-year occupational therapy students: practice with a generative AI simulated patient and an expert demonstration video. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Which teaching method leads to better interview performance in an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) with a standardized patient?
2. How do the two methods affect students' interview self-efficacy?
3. How do students evaluate the two methods, and which learning sequence do they prefer?

Students enrolled in a required vocational rehabilitation course were randomly assigned to one of two sequences. In the first teaching week, one sequence practiced interviewing a GPT-4o-based simulated patient (a 35-year-old person with schizophrenia), and the other watched and discussed an expert demonstration interview of the same case. Both groups completed a 9-minute standardized-patient OSCE on the same day. In the following week, the two sequences crossed over to the other method. Interview self-efficacy was measured before teaching, after the first method, and after the second method.
primary_outcomes: OSCE interview performance score
title: Generative AI Simulated Patients Versus Expert Demonstration Videos for Psychiatric Interview Training in Occupational Therapy Students

brief_summary:
Almost half of critically ill patients experience delirium. Delirium is associated with impaired cognition, mortality, and increased healthcare costs. Family members of critically ill patients are also at risk for adverse consequences such as depression and anxiety.

One strategy that may help to improve outcomes is to engage family members in the prevention, detection, and management of delirium. This study will employ an educational module to educate families on delirium symptoms, how delirium can be identified, and how to prevent and manage delirium using non-pharmacological strategies.

Family member delirium detection may result in earlier and more accurate recognition of delirium as well as meaningful family involvement, and ultimately the potential for better patient and family outcomes. This study aims to determine the efficacy of employing family-administered delirium prevention, detection, and management in the critically ill, compared to standard of care. We hypothesize that family-administered delirium prevention, detection, and management in the critically ill will be superior to standard of care in:

1. Reducing psychological distress in family members,
2. Reducing the prevalence, duration, and severity of delirium in critically ill patients,
3. Increasing delirium identification in medical charts,
4. Increasing delirium knowledge in family members of critically ill patients, and
5. Reducing the burden of delirium experienced by family members and caregivers
conditions: Post Intensive Care Unit Syndrome Family
primary_outcomes: Family member symptoms of depression and anxiety
title: Family-partnered Delirium Prevention, Detection, and Management in the ICU

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether electronic tools that provide information and reminders to people at high risk for breast cancer and their healthcare providers can increase the use of medications, such as tamoxifen, that may help lower the risk of developing breast cancer. The study will also look at how these tools can be successfully used as part of routine medical care.
primary_outcomes: Chemoprevention Uptake
title: Decision Support for Chemoprevention

brief_summary: This prospective single-center observational cohort study investigates whether objectively measured early postoperative heart rate variability (HRV) and sleep parameters are associated with patient-reported quality of recovery after cesarean delivery. Women who deliver by cesarean section wear a consumer wrist device (Garmin Vívosmart 5) on the non-dominant wrist during the in-hospital period (first 48 hours). HRV metrics (e.g., RMSSD), continuous heart rate, and sleep are derived from raw beat-to-beat intervals via the Fitrockr platform. Quality of recovery is measured with the validated Turkish Obstetric Quality-of-Recovery score (ObsQoR-11T) at 24 and 48 hours, and subjective sleep with the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ). The primary hypothesis is that higher early HRV (particularly RMSSD) and better sleep are associated with higher ObsQoR-11T at postoperative day 1 (24 hours). The wearable is used for research purposes only and does not inform any clinical decision; routine care proceeds independently of the study.
interventions: Wearable-derived heart rate variability and sleep monitoring
primary_outcomes: Correlation between early heart rate variability (ln RMSSD) and quality of recovery (ObsQoR-11T)
title: Early Heart Rate Variability and Sleep and Quality of Recovery After Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare microprocessor-controlled knee prostheses in early rehabilitation in amputees with transfemoral amputations and low mobility (K I-II). The main question it aims to answer is:

* Does the Avior knee prosthesis in early rehabilitation improve the mobility and well-being of the patients?
* Is the Avior knee prothesis suitable for use in early rehabilitation?
* Is the Avior knee prothesis suitable for use of amputees with low mobility (K I-II?

Researchers will compare the Avior knee prothesis to the Kenevo knee prothesis to see if the preious results are achieved or surpassed.

Participants will:

* wear the knee protheses to be tested for 6 months
* complete mobility tests during their 6 weeks stay at the rehabilitation facility (every 3 weeks --\> total: 3 times)
* fill out questionairs concerning their mobilty and pain perception
primary_outcomes: Mobility of lower-limb prosthesis users: PLUS-M™ 12-Item Short Form T-score
title: Early Rehabilitation After Transfemoral Amputation in Moderately Active Patients Using the Avior Knee

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy, and safety of AXT-1003 combined with Enzalutamide in subjects with advanced prostate cancer.
primary_outcomes: DLT events
Incidence and severity of AEs and serious AEs (SAEs)
title: AXT-1003 Combination With Enzalutamide in Participants With mCRPC

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study examines whether EEG markers derived from full-night polysomnography (sleep spindle density, K-complex density, and REM EEG slowing) are associated with cognitive performance in adults with obstructive sleep apnea, and whether they explain more variance in cognitive test scores than classical OSA metrics (AHI, T90, minimal SpO2).
interventions: Full-night polysomnography with EEG marker analysis and cognitive testing
lead_sponsor: University of Split, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Correlation between sleep spindle density and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) total score
Correlation between sleep spindle density and Digit Span Test forward score
Correlation between sleep spindle density and Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) mean reaction time
Correlation between sleep spindle density and Trail Making Test Part A (TMT-A) completion time
Correlation between sleep spindle density and Stroop Test interference-condition completion time
Correlation between sleep spindle density and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) score
title: EEG Markers From Polysomnography and Cognitive Performance in Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of an electromagnetic trainer in improving lower limb motor function, gait, and balance in patients after cerebral stroke. The study will include 80 adult patients with a first-ever cerebral stroke who are undergoing medical rehabilitation. Participants will be randomly allocated to two parallel groups. The control group will receive standard medical rehabilitation, while the intervention group will receive standard rehabilitation combined with motor training using an electromagnetic trainer. Clinical and functional assessments will include neurological status, functional independence, gait and balance, lower limb motor function, muscle tone, range of motion, and psycho-emotional status. The study is expected to determine whether the addition of electromagnetic motor training provides greater improvement in functional outcomes compared with standard rehabilitation alone.
primary_outcomes: Berg Balance Scale (BBS)
title: Effect of an Electromagnetic Trainer on Gait and Balance Recovery After Stroke

brief_summary: This clinical trial aims to compare the efficacy of the dual therapy regimen of linralase glutarate capsules and amoxicillin versus the quadruple therapy regimen containing bismuth for the first-line eradication of Helicobacter pylori infection. The primary questions this trial aims to address include: 1. Whether the linalarenate glutarate capsule-amoxicillin dual-drug regimen is non-inferior to the bismuth-containing quadruple therapy, while simultaneously evaluating patient adherence and the incidence of adverse events in both treatment groups. Participants will: 1. Treatment group: Linaralate Glutarate Capsules (50 mg bid) + Amoxicillin (1 g tid), for a 14-day treatment course. 2. Control group: Esomeprazole 20 mg, twice daily (bid) + clarithromycin 0.5 g, twice daily (bid) + amoxicillin 1 g, twice daily (bid) + colloidal bismuth subcitrate 200 mg, twice daily (bid), for a 14-day treatment course. The primary endpoint is the Helicobacter pylori eradication rate 4 weeks after discontinuation of treatment.
primary_outcomes: Helicobacter pylori eradication
title: Efficacy and Safety of Linarazen Gluconate Capsules Combined With Amoxicillin (Dual-Drug Therapy) Versus Bismuth-Containing Quadruple Therapy for First-Line Eradication of Helicobacter Pylori Infection

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if adding small ear needles to a standard oral medicine can ease symptoms in adults with early-stage internal hemorrhoids (swollen blood vessels inside the anus, grade I-II) who also have the "heat-toxin syndrome" of traditional medicine. In this pattern, people typically have bright red bleeding when passing stool, a burning feeling in the anus, dry stool, dark yellow urine, a dry throat with a bitter taste, a red tongue with a greasy yellow coating, and a rapid pulse. The trial will also learn about the safety of the ear needles.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does adding ear needles to the standard medicine lower anal discomfort or pain during bowel movements after 14 days? Does it also reduce bleeding and prolapse (hemorrhoids that come out of the anus) and improve quality of life? What side effects do participants have with the ear needles and with the medicine?

Researchers will compare two groups to see if the ear needles help beyond the standard medicine alone. One group will receive ear needles and the other will receive look-alike ear patches with the needle removed (a "sham" treatment, used so that participants cannot tell which treatment they received). Both groups will take the same medicine, diosmin/hesperidin (Daflon 500 mg), and receive the same diet and lifestyle advice.

Participants will:

Take Daflon 500 mg tablets for 14 days Have ear needles or sham patches placed on seven points of one ear on Day 0 and Day 7 (switching ears each time), and have them removed on Day 5 and Day 12 Press the needles or patches gently at least 3 times a day for 1 minute each time Visit the clinic on Day 0, Day 7 and Day 14 to report their pain (on a 0-10 scale), bleeding and prolapse, and to complete a quality-of-life questionnaire (Day 0 and Day 14) Report any side effects to the study team

brief_summary:
Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health issue. Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is one of the indicators that is monitored particularly closely. In animals, pig farms, among others, have been identified as reservoirs of MRSA, with a risk of transmission to humans, particularly to individuals in direct contact with livestock. In France, the prevalence of MRSA in pig farms has increased markedly in recent years.

While cross-species transmission between pigs and humans in professional settings is well-documented, the temporal dynamics, the actual incidence of acquisition, and the associated determinants remain insufficiently characterized in France.

Adopting a "One Health" approach, this project aims to gain a better understanding of the mechanisms by which MRSA spreads between animal and human subpopulations and to incorporate these insights into a mathematical modeling framework.

brief_summary:
Cesarean section is the most common inpatient surgical procedure worldwide, with rates continuing to rise; in Canada, approximately one in three births occur by cesarean. Despite its prevalence, there are no expectations for individuals who have undergone a cesarean section to seek out rehabilitation care. Physical recovery guidance and return to activity from a cesarean birth is poorly understood and inadequately supported, with most research focusing on immediate post-operative pain management within the hospital settings. Little attention has been given to long term physical recovery.

Scar-related problems - such as tight or stuck scar tissue, sensitivity or discomfort around the scar, weakness in the abdominal muscles, and infertility or digestive complications - can severely affects the ability to complete daily activities and affect overall quality of life. Rehabilitation is a common and important part of recovery after most major orthopedic and abdominal surgeries. It can help reduce pain and complications, improve mobility, strength, and confidence in movement, and support a gradual return to physical activity. Just as importantly, rehabilitation helps individuals safely resume everyday responsibilities such as caring for their family, returning to work, and managing daily tasks.

The purpose of this study is to examine whether one form of hands-on therapy results in greater improvements in scar comfort, mobility, and performance of daily activities compared with an alternative approach, when both are delivered alongside an identical exercise program.

Participants will take part in an 8-week rehabilitation program following cesarean birth. Rehabilitation will be provided one-on-one by a qualified healthcare professional and will include a combination of in-person sessions and virtual (online) check-ins. In-person sessions will include education about recovery, hands-on therapy, and guided exercises. Virtual sessions will be used to answer questions, review progress, and ensure that exercises are being performed safely and correctly at home.

To evaluate changes in recovery over time, participants will attend three assessment sessions: at baseline (week 0), mid-intervention (week 4), and post-intervention (week 8). During these sessions, researchers will collect information on:

* How the scar looks and moves
* The sensitivity or discomfort of the scar area
* How easily participants can perform everyday movements, such as standing up from a chair
* How participants feel about their scar, pain levels, and daily function There will be two forms off assessments. One that measures the objective changes: photographs of the scar, gentle pressure testing to measure sensitivity, simple movement tests, and ultrasound imaging, while the other form of assessment is patient reported questionnaires about how they feel they are improving. Ultrasound is a safe and painless technique that allows researchers to see how tissues under the skin are healing and moving.

The anticipated benefit of this research is to improve understanding of physical recovery after cesarean birth. The results may help inform future rehabilitation recommendations and contribute to better support for individuals recovering from cesarean surgery.

brief_summary:
Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold-standard treatment for patients with end-stage heart failure refractory to the medical management, offering the best survival and quality of life.

In the absence of a reliable non-invasive biomarker, international guidelines recommend to screen for cardiac allograft rejection during the first-year post-transplant using iterative protocol endomyocardial biopsies, a stressful and invasive procedure at risk of periprocedural complications. This invasive strategy suffers from multiple limitations and is increasingly being questioned.

Recently, circulating donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) ""Donor-derived cell-FreE Deoxyribonucleic Acid"", has been proposed as a reliable non-invasive biomarker of rejection in solid organ transplantation. Strong associations between allograft rejection and dd-cfDNA have been found in observational studies.

Although donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is considered as the most promising non-invasive biomarker of allograft injury by international experts, no interventional trial has ever confirmed the efficiency and the safety of the non-invasive monitoring of rejection using dd-cfDNA. This prospective validation is mandatory and represents an important unmet medical need.We hypothesize that a non-invasive dd-cfDNA-based strategy might be superior to an invasive biopsy-based strategy for the screening of rejection in terms of patients' survival, allograft function and quality of life.

brief_summary:
Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a life-threatening heart rhythm disorder that frequently occurs in patients with structural heart disease, such as ischemic or non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. In these patients, VT usually arises from re-entrant circuits within or around scar tissue in the heart muscle. Catheter ablation, which uses radiofrequency energy to eliminate the abnormal tissue responsible for VT, is an established treatment. However, its long-term success rate remains modest (about 40-60%), partly because conventional three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping (EAM) relies on voltage measurements that cannot fully reveal the complex three-dimensional scar architecture that drives the arrhythmia.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) can visualize myocardial scar in high detail before the procedure. Dedicated software (ADAS-3D) converts these MRI scans into a patient-specific three-dimensional model of the scar, including the "heterogeneous tissue channels" of surviving muscle within the scar that are the likely source of VT. This model can be integrated into the mapping system during the ablation procedure, potentially allowing operators to identify and treat the critical tissue more precisely.

This prospective, multi-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial is testing whether adding LGE-MRI guidance to conventional electrical mapping improves the outcomes of VT ablation. Adults aged 18 to 75 years with structural heart disease and documented sustained VT will undergo cardiac MRI screening. Those with visible scar (LGE-positive) will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two groups: ablation guided by LGE-MRI integrated with electroanatomical mapping (experimental group), or ablation guided by electroanatomical mapping alone without image integration (control group, with operators blinded to the MRI findings). Patients without scar on MRI will be followed in a separate observational registry.

All participants will be monitored in hospital for at least 24 hours after the procedure and will attend clinic visits at 3, 6, and 12 months. VT recurrence will be monitored with wearable smart ECG devices (worn for at least 7 days at each follow-up) and, in patients with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD), by device interrogation. The main goal of the study is to determine whether MRI-guided ablation reduces the combined risk of VT recurrence, cardiovascular hospitalization, or death during 12 months of follow-up compared with standard ablation. The study also assesses procedure-related complications.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Composite of ventricular tachycardia recurrence, cardiovascular hospitalization, or death
title: MRI-guided Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in Patients With Structural Heart Disease

brief_summary:
Beta-blockers have shown promise as a treatment to improve patient prognosis following traumatic brain injury (TBI), although the exact mechanism by which they might confer this benefit remains unknown.

At the clinical level, several retrospective cohort studies, prospective cohort studies, small prospective clinical trials, and various reviews and meta-analyses suggest that beta-blockers may be associated with an improved prognosis in patients with TBI. Furthermore, the optimal timing, dosage, and duration of beta-blocker treatment remain uncertain. This means there is still uncertainty regarding the overall efficacy of beta-blockade in patients with TBI, as well as the specifics of patient selection, drugs, dosages, routes of administration, and physiological targets.

In summary, the use of beta-blockers in patients with TBI appears to be associated with reduced mortality at the time of ICU discharge, as well as better long-term functional outcomes. However, the lack of high-quality scientific evidence clearly limits the ability to make a generalized recommendation regarding the use of beta-blockers in these patients. Therefore, further clinical trials are needed to analyze the effect of beta-blockers on mortality and short- and long-term functional outcomes in patients with TBI admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

primary_outcomes: In-hospital mortality

brief_summary:
Cervicogenic headache is a secondary headache disorder associated with dysfunction of the cervical spine and surrounding muscles. It may cause neck pain, muscle tenderness, recurrent headaches, and limitations in daily activities, ultimately affecting quality of life. The study aimed to determine whether Strain Counterstrain (SCS) or Post-Isometric Relaxation (PIR) produces better outcomes in reducing pain intensity, decreasing headache frequency, and improving headache-related quality of life.

A randomized clinical trial was conducted in the Physiotherapy Department of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Lahore, involving 34 female participants who were randomly allocated into two equal groups of 17 participants each. Group A received Strain Counterstrain, while Group B received Post-Isometric Relaxation. Strain Counterstrain is a passive manual therapy technique in which the therapist positions the affected cervical tissues in a comfortable position to reduce tenderness and abnormal muscle activity.

Participants were assessed using three outcome measures: the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) to measure pain intensity, a Headache Frequency Diary to record headache episodes, and the Headache Impact Test (HIT-6) to assess the effect of headaches on daily functioning and quality of life. Assessments were conducted at baseline, after six weeks, and at twelve weeks, as reported in the results section.

The study aimed to determine whether Strain Counterstrain (SCS) or Post-Isometric Relaxation (PIR) produces better outcomes in reducing pain intensity, decreasing headache frequency, and improving headache-related quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Pain Measured by Numeric Pain Rating Scale
Headache episode measured by the Headache Frequency Diary
title: Effects of Strain Counterstrain Versus Post Isometric Relaxation on Pain, Headache Frequency, and Quality of Life in Females With Cervicogenic Headache.

The study involved 144 caregiver-child pairs at a tertiary hospital in Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Caregivers' first-aid knowledge and skills were assessed at the beginning of the study and again at 4 and 12 weeks. The main outcome was caregivers' ability to correctly demonstrate nosebleed first aid at 12 weeks. Other outcomes included first-aid knowledge, the number and duration of nosebleeds, whether bleeding could be stopped at home within 15 minutes, and unplanned healthcare visits.

The study aimed to determine whether a brief, structured nursing education program could help families manage recurrent childhood nosebleeds more effectively.

brief_summary:
The bacteria and other microorganisms that naturally live in the gut (the gut microbiome) play an important role in a baby's early development. Babies born by cesarean section are exposed to different microorganisms at birth than babies born vaginally, which may affect the normal establishment of the gut microbiome.Early changes in the gut microbiome can affect the development and function of the immune system, as well as metabolism and gut function, and may increase the risk of certain diseases later in life. They have also been associated with infant colic, a common condition that may be related to increased sensitivity to abdominal pain.

Current approaches to restore the gut microbiome after cesarean birth, such as transferring the mother's vaginal or fecal microbiota, raise important safety concerns. This study aims to better understand how differences in the early gut microbiome influence gut development, immune function, and pain sensitivity, and to identify naturally occurring beneficial bacteria that could provide a safer alternative.

To achieve this, the researchers will study stool samples from newborns delivered vaginally or by cesarean section. Gut bacteria will be isolated and characterized in the laboratory, and selected microorganisms will be evaluated in preclinical models to better understand their effects on gut and immune development. The findings may support the development of new probiotic approaches to promote healthy gut microbiome development in infants born by cesarean section and reduce the long-term health consequences of early microbiome disruption.

brief_summary:
Background:

The prevalence of sedative-hypnotic use among middle-aged and older adults in Taiwan has continued to rise, highlighting the need to better understand the underlying factors contributing to sleep disturbances and medication dependence. Emerging evidence suggests that, beyond psychological and behavioral contributors, age-related physiological decline may play an important role. Sarcopenia, characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and strength, is common in aging populations and has been linked to poor sleep quality, daytime fatigue, increased fall risk, and higher medication use. Regular physical activity not only improves symptoms of sarcopenia but has also been shown to enhance subjective sleep quality and modify objective sleep architecture, including increases in N3 slow-wave sleep. Despite these benefits, no study to date has directly examined whether physical activity can facilitate sedative-hypnotic dose reduction among chronic users.

Purpose:

The aim of this study is to investigate the associations among sarcopenia, sleep disturbances, and sedative-hypnotic use, and to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured physical activity intervention in improving subjective and objective sleep outcomes and promoting dose reduction in chronic hypnotic users.

Methods:

This three-year study will recruit 180 adults aged 50 years and older who have long-term sedative-hypnotic use. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an individualized 12-week physical activity program or a relaxation training control condition. Baseline and post-intervention assessments will include subjective sleep questionnaires, polysomnography, muscle strength and mass measurements, and standardized hypnotic dose quantification.

Expected Results:

Investigators anticipate that physical activity targeting muscle health will significantly improve sleep quality and contribute to meaningful reductions in sedative-hypnotic medication use among chronic users.
primary_outcomes: Daily Dose equivalent for statistical purpose (S-DDD)
title: Physical Activity Interventions for Sleep Improvement and Sedative-Hypnotic Reduction in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: Investigating the Role of Sarcopenia

brief_summary: Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults in rural China. This study evaluated whether a village doctor-delivered fall prevention program, integrated into the national Basic Public Health Services, could reduce falls among community-dwelling older adults aged 60-79 years at high risk of falling in rural Chongqing. In this cluster randomized controlled trial, 8 villages were randomly assigned to either a multicomponent fall prevention intervention (health education, home-based balance and strength exercises, and home environment modification guidance, delivered by village doctors through classroom sessions and home visits) or usual care with printed fall prevention materials. A total of 320 participants were followed for 12 months. Falls, fall-related injuries, and fall prevention knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) were assessed.
lead_sponsor: Chongqing Center for Disease Control and Prevention
primary_outcomes: 12-month fall incidence (proportion with at least one fall)
title: Village Doctor-Delivered Fall Prevention Program for Older Adults in Rural Chongqing

brief_summary:
This study aimed to investigate the effects of an eight-week exercise training program on posture, pain, and sleep quality in esports players.

Esports players were randomly assigned to an exercise group or a control group. Participants in the exercise group performed a home-based exercise program consisting of postural exercises, stretching, spinal mobility exercises, and breathing exercises. The control group did not receive structured exercise training. Both groups received recommendations regarding ergonomic sitting posture and physical activity.

Posture, pain, disability related to neck and low back pain, and sleep quality were assessed at baseline and after eight weeks using the New York Posture Rating Chart, Visual Analog Scale, Neck Disability Index, Oswestry Disability Index, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index.
primary_outcomes: Posture
Pain Intensity
Neck-Related Disability
Low Back-Related Disability
Sleep Quality
title: Effects of Exercise Training on Posture, Pain, and Sleep Quality in Esports Players

brief_summary:
Diabetic macular edema is an eye condition caused by diabetes in which fluid accumulates in the central part of the retina, leading to blurred vision and potentially permanent vision loss. Bevacizumab is a medicine that blocks vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a protein involved in abnormal leakage from blood vessels. It is commonly used as an injection into the eye to treat this condition.

This study aims to compare two methods of delivering bevacizumab in patients with center-involving diabetic macular edema. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The first group will receive bevacizumab injections into the vitreous cavity of the eye (intravitreal injection), while the second group will receive injections into the space between the sclera and choroid of the eye (suprachoroidal injection). Both groups will receive injections once a month for three months.

The study will compare changes in vision and central retinal thickness, measured using an eye examination and optical coherence tomography (OCT), from the start of the study to the four-month assessment. The occurrence of treatment-related complications and other adverse events will also be recorded.

The study hypothesis is that suprachoroidal bevacizumab will provide improvements in vision and retinal thickness comparable to intravitreal bevacizumab, with a potentially different safety profile. The findings may help determine whether suprachoroidal delivery is a useful alternative to the established intravitreal route for treating diabetic macular edema.
primary_outcomes: Central Macular Thickness
Visual Acuity
title: Suprachoroidal Bevacizumab Versus Intravitreal Bevacizumab in Diabetic Macular Edema

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a behavioral program called I'M Walking will help with pain in middle-aged and older adults.

* Does the program improve pain interference in participants with knee osteoarthritis?
* What other factors may affect pain interference with participants that did the intervention?

Researchers will compare the I'M Walking program with a Walk With Ease program (self-directed program)
lead_sponsor: Weill Medical College of Cornell University
primary_outcomes: Difference between groups in pain interference as measured by PROMIS Pain Interference (PI) Short Form 8a at week 24
title: Study Comparing Osteoarthritis Programs

brief_summary:
This study evaluated how trained young male football players responded to two high-intensity interval training (HIIT) sessions that differed in the length of the passive recovery period between repeated running bouts. Participants completed both exercise conditions in a fixed order. The first session used 10 seconds of high-intensity running followed by 10 seconds of passive recovery (HIIT 1:1). Seven days later, the same participants completed a second session using 10 seconds of high-intensity running followed by 20 seconds of passive recovery (HIIT 1:2).

Both exercise sessions were matched for exercise intensity, active work duration, number of repetitions, and prescribed running distance. Participants were assessed before exercise, immediately after exercise, and at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours after each session.

The study examined biochemical responses, perceived muscle soreness, countermovement jump performance, and changes in circulating amino acids and amino acid-related compounds. The purpose was to describe and compare recovery responses across the two fixed-sequence HIIT sessions. Because all participants completed HIIT 1:1 first and HIIT 1:2 second, the study was not randomized or counterbalanced, and any differences between sessions may also reflect session-order effects.
conditions: Exercise Recovery Following High-Intensity Interval Training
High-Intensity Interval Training in Football Players
primary_outcomes: Perceived Lower-Extremity Muscle Soreness Score
title: Amino-Acid and Recovery Responses Across Two Fixed-Sequence HIIT Sessions in Trained Male Football Players

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how ashwagandha, a herbal dietary supplement, affects quality of life in women with endometriosis. Researchers will also assess how well participants tolerate it.

The main questions are:

* Does ashwagandha affect mental well-being and quality of life compared with placebo?
* Does it affect physical health, perceived stress, or endometriosis-related quality of life?
* Does it affect pain during intercourse or how participants manage pain, including pain medication use?
* What side effects or changes in blood test results occur during supplementation?

Researchers will compare ashwagandha with a placebo, a look-alike capsule containing no active ingredient. The study will include 90 women. A chance process will assign participants to a group. Each participant has a two-in-three chance of receiving ashwagandha. Neither participants nor researchers assessing the results will know who receives ashwagandha during this phase.

Participants will:

* Take 300 mg of ashwagandha or placebo daily for 12 weeks. This may extend to 16 weeks to match assessments with the menstrual cycle.
* Complete questionnaires about quality of life, stress, pain during intercourse, and pain management.
* Attend regular clinic visits for health checks and blood tests.
* Attend a follow-up visit about four weeks after finishing the study capsules.

After the first phase, eligible participants may choose to continue for another 12 weeks. Everyone in this optional phase will take ashwagandha and know they are taking it. Researchers will track further changes in quality of life, stress, and side effects.

Participants will continue their usual care for endometriosis. Whether ashwagandha benefits women with endometriosis is not yet known.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) Mental Component Summary (MCS) score
title: Effects of Ashwagandha Supplementation on Quality of Life and Well-Being in Women With Endometriosis

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to learn whether a handheld, non-invasive stimulation device called gammaCore Emerald can change brain activity and thinking skills. Researchers will use MRI scans to measure changes in brain activity after stimulation and compare the results among people with schizophrenia, depression, and healthy volunteers.
primary_outcomes: functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI)
title: Non-Invasive Vagus Nerve Stimulation as a Probe to Map Functional Connectivity in Schizophrenia Using Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effects of heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB), mindfulness meditation, and psychological education in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients waiting for TKA often experience anxiety, pain, and sleep problems before surgery. These factors may affect recovery after surgery. HRVB and mindfulness have been used to reduce stress and anxiety in different patient groups, but few studies have directly compared these approaches in patients undergoing TKA.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does HRVB improve postoperative recovery, including pain, sleep quality, quality of life, and knee function, compared with mindfulness meditation and psychological education?
* Do HRVB and mindfulness meditation reduce preoperative anxiety more effectively than psychological education?
* Are changes in heart rate variability and EEG measures related to recovery outcomes after surgery?

Researchers will compare HRVB, mindfulness meditation, and psychological education to evaluate their effects on anxiety reduction and postoperative recovery.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of three groups: HRVB, mindfulness meditation, or psychological education.
* Receive one 15-minute intervention session before surgery.
* Continue home-based practice during the first 2 weeks after surgery while following routine rehabilitation exercises.
* Complete assessments before surgery and at 2, 6, and 12 weeks after surgery.

The assessments will include measures of anxiety, pain, sleep quality, quality of life, knee function, heart rate variability, and EEG activity.
primary_outcomes: Visual Analogue Scale change
Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)
Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)
EuroQol-5D questionnaire (EQ-5D)
title: A Comparison of Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback, Mindfulness, and Psychoeducation-based Interventions on Clinical Recovery Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary: Management of children's dental fear (CDF) typically relies on conventional one-on-one isolated behavioral interventions delivered by individual clinicians at the chairside. However, these traditional approaches often fail to address fundamental organizational and systemic issues, such as the lack of standardized pre-treatment assessment tools, inadequate systematic training for clinical staff, and insufficient sustained family engagement. To tackle these challenges, our team initiated a quality control circle (QCC) project aimed at reducing the prevalence of CDF among preschool children.
primary_outcomes: The prevalence of children's dental fear.
title: QCC Intervention for Dental Fear in Preschool Children: A Non-Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether practical episiotomy training using simulation models improves midwifery students' confidence in their ability to perform the procedure, their confidence in learning, and their satisfaction with the training.

An episiotomy is a surgical cut made in the area between the vaginal opening and the anus during childbirth when medically necessary. Proper repair of this cut and any tears that may occur during childbirth is important for maternal health. Therefore, midwifery students need to develop appropriate knowledge and skills before graduation. Practicing on simulation models may help students gain experience and confidence in a safe learning environment before performing procedures on real patients.

The study will be conducted among third-year midwifery students at the Faculty of Health Sciences, Kırklareli University, Türkiye. Students aged 18 years or older who are taking the Childbirth Knowledge III course for the first time will be eligible to participate. Approximately 90-100 students are expected to take part. Participation will be voluntary.

Students who agree to participate will be randomly assigned by computer to one of two groups. The first group will receive standard episiotomy education, including a presentation and an educational video. The second group will receive the same standard education plus hands-on practice using special episiotomy simulation models. Practical training will be conducted in small groups under the guidance of the researchers.

Before training, all students will complete a questionnaire about their background and educational experience, as well as questions assessing how confident they feel in their ability to perform episiotomy-related procedures. Immediately after training, students will complete questionnaires assessing their satisfaction with the education and their confidence in learning. One month later, their perceived ability to perform episiotomy-related procedures will be assessed again. After all assessments are completed, students in the standard education group will also be offered the opportunity to practice using simulation models.

No procedures will be performed on real patients as part of this study. Participants' information will be kept confidential and used only for scientific purposes. Students may withdraw from the study at any time.

The study will examine whether adding hands-on simulation training to standard education improves students' confidence, perceived ability, and satisfaction with learning. The findings may help improve midwifery education and contribute to better quality maternity care in the future.
primary_outcomes: Change in Episiotomy Self-Efficacy
title: Model-Based Episiotomy Training

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the efficacy of preoperative nebulized lignocaine versus nebulized dexmedetomidine for blunting the pressor response to laryngoscopy and intubation in patients with controlled hypertension under medical treatment.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of blunting Pressor Response to Laryngoscopy
title: Preoperative Nebulized Lignocaine Versus Nebulized Dexmedetomidine for Blunting the Pressor Response to Laryngoscopy and Intubation in Controlled Hypertensive Patients

brief_summary: Lack of effective interventions to improve diet quality among older urban adults represents a significant health problem. Simultaneously, enhancing the biomedical workforce is needed to meet growing US demands in research and science fields to address disparities in chronic disease outcomes. This project meets these demands by expanding research training opportunities for younger students to build confidence and self-efficacy that they belong in an academic research environment, while providing a relatively low-cost nutrition intervention to disseminate to help narrow these gaps.
primary_outcomes: Dietary quality
title: Nutrition Intervention for Older Adults and Research Training
